The panel can reconnect any runtime's server (r, which the daemon passes to the runtime that hosts it), and toggle enablement and add, edit, or remove definitions of global-runtime servers only; a coding runtime's servers come from its runtime template. Add/edit forms accept either a command, JSON string array of arguments, JSON string object of environment variables, and optional working directory, or a URL plus a JSON string object of headers. Choose runtime only or user config.toml before submitting. Edits do not rename a server; remove the old name and add the new one instead.

Stdio servers negotiate MCP 2025-11-25 when needed. Servers that implement the 2026-07-28 discovery lifecycle use that version. Remote servers use Streamable HTTP, including SSE responses on that endpoint; the retired two-endpoint legacy SSE transport is not supported.

docs.title: Repository security
docs.text:
There is no separate MCP trust store or approval prompt. Every configured, enabled server connects eagerly. MCP tools are permission-gated like normal tools: an agent with no mcp permission entry cannot see them, and scoped rules decide each call.

MCP servers and agent documents come only from your user configuration; a repository's .cookie-agent/config.toml and .cookie-agent/agents/ are never read, so opening a repository cannot add a server or an agent that permits its tools. Repository AGENTS.md files and project skills still enter model context; review them in repositories you do not trust.

Connection failures are isolated per server. A failed server publishes no tools and does not prevent other servers from connecting (see Connection lifecycle).

Definitions created or changed through the TUI are runtime-layer entries and live only for the current daemon unless explicitly written to a file. After a write-back the file holds the entry, and it is no longer a runtime entry.

docs.title: Tool names and permissions
docs.text:
An MCP tool is exposed as <server>_<tool>. Both components replace characters outside [a-zA-Z0-9_-] with _; there is no mcp_ prefix. For example, github plus search/repos becomes github_search_repos. Inside the global runtime, a server whose generated name collides with another MCP or plugin tool, or with the global webfetch, is rejected; inside a coding runtime, one that collides with another of its MCP servers' tools or its built-in tools is rejected the same way, and the built-in tools keep their names. A name that collides with a tool of another runtime or of the base layer is published with the runtime's attachment prefix instead, for example global_github_search_repos or labpc_api_rust_analyzer_hover; see tool composition.

permissions:
  mcp:
    "github_*": allow
    github_delete_repo: deny

MCP availability is permission-driven. With no mcp entry, an agent receives no MCP tools; deny-only mcp rules also hide them. Any mcp allow or ask rule in the agent or overlay exposes the connected MCP tools at the action level. Calls then use the complete generated tool name as their scoped resource: more-specific patterns override broader patterns, and unmatched calls are denied. Each delegated agent is evaluated against its own permission map.

Each MCP description and result is treated as untrusted server output.

Media blocks in tool results (images, audio, and embedded resource blobs) are sniffed by content, gated on the model's capabilities and the provider's delivery channel exactly like media reads, and retained as content-addressed attachments. Gated media fails the tool call with an actionable error; malformed blocks degrade to inline notes. Blob resources without a declared MIME type are retained under the sniffed type. Results that would exceed the combined attachment budget keep what fits and degrade the remainder to inline notes.

docs.title: Accepted fields
docs.text:
These are the complete fields under [mcp.servers.<name>]. File precedence is described in config.toml.

Key Type Default Description command string (none) Stdio server executable. Exactly one of command or url is required. args array of strings empty Command arguments; valid only with command. env map of strings empty Command environment additions; valid only with command. cwd string (none) Child working directory; valid only with command. url string (none) Absolute HTTP or HTTPS Streamable HTTP endpoint. Exactly one of url or command is required. headers map of strings empty Static request headers; valid only with url. oauth boolean or table auto Streamable HTTP OAuth. Omit, set true, or use {} for reactive OAuth; set false to disable it. A table accepts optional client_id, client_secret, client_metadata_url, and scopes. A static Authorization header takes precedence. enabled boolean true Whether the server may connect. timeout_ms integer 30000 Positive timeout for connect, list, and call operations.

docs.title: Runtime layers and persistence
docs.text:
The running engine adds a mutable Runtime layer for MCP server entries. It wins over the user file and lasts for the daemon lifetime. Runtime removals are tombstones: the named server is absent even when the user file defines it. Runtime and user-file entries use the same connection lifecycle. Nothing is written automatically.

Explicit MCP write-back (mcp.server.persist) replaces only [mcp.servers.<name>] in the user config.toml, or removes it for a runtime removal, using a format-preserving TOML document edit, as a configuration change. Unrelated keys, tables, and comments are retained. The complete candidate, with the agent documents beside it, is passed through the strict configuration loader before an atomic replacement; an existing unknown field, type conflict, or malformed table fails without changing the file. The replacement syncs the candidate before rename and syncs the containing directory afterward. The newly staged replacement is owner-only; the existing source path is not validated before replacement. The source file is re-read and compared immediately before replacement, and a mismatch fails with a conflict instead of overwriting the external edit. A modification landing between that comparison and the rename itself cannot be detected — a narrow residual race that only matters if another writer edits the file in the same instant; avoid concurrent external edits while applying changes. A successful write applies the configuration, and the server's entry comes from the file from then on.

docs.title: Plugins [plugins]
docs.text:
Plugins are local programs that extend Cookie Agent from their own process. A plugin can declare tools, intercept engine hooks, watch session events, publish to a bus other plugins hear, and send messages to sessions. Install a plugin by getting its executable from its author and adding it to your configuration.

To write a plugin, see Plugin development.

docs.title: Configure a plugin
docs.text:
Configure each plugin under [plugins.<name>] in the user config.toml (~/.cookie-agent/config.toml). Names must be nonempty, at most 128 bytes, and contain no control characters.

[plugins.issues]
command = ["/opt/cookie-plugins/issues", "--stdio"]
env = { ISSUES_URL = "https://issues.example.com" }
cwd = "/workspace"
enabled = true
producer_messaging = false
interception_timeout_ms = 2000
startup_timeout_ms = 10000
shutdown_grace_ms = 3000

command is the program and its arguments, as for a runtime. The plugin's process inherits the daemon's environment, like an MCP stdio server, and env adds to it, overriding inherited variables of the same name. A plugin therefore also sees provider API keys and other secrets the daemon reads from its environment.

Each enabled plugin starts with the daemon. Set enabled = false to keep a plugin configured without starting it. Configuration changes take effect when the daemon next starts. Plugins run their hooks in the order the file lists them.

Key Type Default Description command array of strings (required) The program and its arguments. env map of strings empty Additions to the inherited environment; a listed variable overrides the inherited value. cwd string (none) The process's working directory. enabled boolean true Whether the plugin starts with the daemon. producer_messaging boolean false Lets the plugin register producers and send messages to sessions. interception_timeout_ms integer 2000 How long one hook may take. startup_timeout_ms integer 10000 How long the plugin may take to start and answer plugin/initialize. shutdown_grace_ms integer 3000 How long the plugin may take to exit before it is killed.

Plugin entries reject unknown fields. command must name a program, cwd must be nonempty when set, and every timeout must be greater than zero. These rules apply to disabled entries too.

Plugins are defined only in the user config.toml; a <cwd>/.cookie-agent/config.toml is never read.

docs.title: Plugin tools
docs.text:
A plugin's tools join the daemon's global runtime, next to its MCP servers' tools, and reach every session that keeps global attached. A tool keeps the name the plugin gives it unless another tool has that name; then each is published under its source's prefix, such as issues_search for the issues plugin's search. A plugin may declare a tool an override instead: it keeps the bare name and the other tool is prefixed. The daemon's base tools, such as skill, are never overridden.

A plugin tool is approved like any other tool. Its plugin names the permission action it needs, such as issue_read, and the resource a call works on; a tool may need no permission. Allow the action in an agent's policy or a session overlay:

permissions:
  issue_read: allow
  issue_close:
    "*": ask

The plugin's author should document its actions. See Permissions for policy precedence and session overrides.

docs.title: Status and restarts
docs.text:
Open /plugins in the TUI to see every configured plugin: its state, the tools and hooks it declares, why it last failed, and what it last wrote to standard error. Press r to restart the selected plugin.

State Meaning disabled Configured with enabled = false. starting The process is starting or answering plugin/initialize. connected Running. reconnecting It exited or its connection dropped; the daemon restarts it after 1 s, 2 s, and 4 s. failed Every attempt failed. It stays failed until you restart it. stopped Stopped with the daemon.

A failing plugin never stops the daemon or other plugins. While a plugin is not connected, its tools are not published and its hooks are skipped, unless the plugin declared that a hook blocks when it fails: a policy plugin may, so that what it guards (a tool call, an input, a fork) is refused while it is down instead of going on unchecked. A refusal names the plugin; restart it from /plugins. A plugin's standard error is kept as a short tail (the last 32 lines, at most 4 KiB) rather than shown on the terminal.

At shutdown, the daemon asks each plugin to stop, waits shutdown_grace_ms, and then kills its process group.

docs.title: Producer messages
docs.text:
A plugin with producer_messaging = true can send messages to any session: steer messages reach the next safe model request, and queue messages start or join a later run. Enable it only for plugins you trust to talk to your models. Sending to an idle session can start a run. A send is acknowledged once the message is durably accepted, not once a model has read it or an external action has finished.

A plugin can discard a message it sent while the message is still waiting. Once a model request claims the message, discard is rejected until the claim is released; consumed messages cannot be discarded.

When it starts, and after every restart, a producing plugin restores its pending work from its own storage and then reports itself ready or failed. session.producers shows each plugin's readiness as starting, ready, failed, or disabled. A goal waits while a plugin it hears from is starting, and work a failed or disabled plugin owned is unknown, never complete. The daemon cannot tell a plugin with no pending work from one that lost its state, so recovery is only as complete as the plugin's own records. See Producers.

docs.title: Trust
docs.text: Plugin commands are trusted local code, not a sandbox. A plugin runs with your user's rights, sees the daemon's environment, and its hooks see and may change prompts, tool calls, and model requests. Tool permissions govern its tools, not its hooks. See security boundaries.

docs.title: Providers [providers]
docs.text: Use /connect for a catalog-backed provider, or define a custom endpoint and model below. Provider configuration lives under [providers.<id>] in config.toml. The authored map defaults to empty; managed providers can still be available through the catalog and user provider store.

docs.title: Managed providers
docs.text:
/connect in the TUI, or cookie connect --token <TOKEN> against the daemon (or set COOKIE_DAEMON_TOKEN), walks through provider setup and authentication: choose the auth method, fill in its setup values (a region, project, or resource name, shown and pre-filled from the stored connection), then type the credentials, which are masked. Connections are stored in the daemon's provider store (~/.cookie-agent/providers/ on the daemon's machine), not in config.toml. Setup is validated locally; the first model request tests the credentials. A failed connect keeps what you typed in the TUI's form, so it can be corrected and resent; a connect that raced a catalog refresh is retried once when the provider's form did not change. Errors name the cause, such as missing_setup_field, missing_credential, or custom_provider_not_store_backed for a [providers.*] provider. Never commit credential-bearing files.

At startup, the engine serves the validated catalog cache (or the bundled catalog on first run) and refreshes https://models.dev/catalog.json in the background right away, then hourly. Supported, non-deprecated text-output models are included automatically. Catalog declarations are not probes of your endpoint: account access, deployed model features, and billing may differ. Models the catalog lists without tool calling are unsupported: they are listed as unavailable with the reason no tool calling and are never selectable, by any agent. Claude on Vertex AI (the google-vertex-anthropic provider and any model routed to @ai-sdk/google-vertex/anthropic) is unsupported: it needs the Anthropic Messages rawPredict wire, which cookie-agent does not implement.

This is a complete config.toml alternative to /connect, with credentials supplied by the environment:

[providers.openai]
source = "models_dev"
api_key = "${env:OPENAI_API_KEY}"

Authored api_key or auth_override takes precedence over an eligible saved connection, then no-auth access, otherwise the provider is unavailable. No-auth access applies to a catalog provider that declares no credential variable, and to a local server: an authored provider whose endpoint (base_url, else the catalog API URL) is on localhost, 127.0.0.1, or ::1. Local catalog providers such as LM Studio stay unavailable until authored, so [providers.lmstudio] with source = "models_dev" is enough to use a running LM Studio. An authored base_url cannot inherit store credentials or setup. Endpoint selection uses authored base_url, catalog API URL, then family default; setup-derived families retain their own routing.

Some catalog providers mix wires: zenmux, ofox, and opencode serve Anthropic, Gemini, or Responses models next to OpenAI-compatible Chat ones, and a model may pin its own catalog API URL. An authored base_url replaces the provider-level API URL, and each model's endpoint follows these rules:

  • A model without its own API URL, or with the provider's, uses base_url.
  • A model API URL on the provider API's origin is rebased by path. With zenmux's https://zenmux.ai/api/v1 and an Anthropic model at https://zenmux.ai/api/anthropic/v1, base_url = "https://gw.example/api/v1" sends that model to https://gw.example/api/anthropic/v1.
  • When base_url does not end with the provider's differing path suffix (v1 above), it is a gateway with its own layout and every model uses base_url itself, whatever its wire (/chat/completions, /messages, /responses, ...).
  • A model API URL on another origin is a separate upstream and is kept.

To send a single model somewhere else, define it in a custom provider.

docs.title: Unavailable models
docs.text:
A catalog model that cookie cannot run stays visible with its reason instead of disappearing. A model is unavailable when it is:

  • quarantined: its models.dev record failed validation (for example invalid_catalog_model_record);
  • unsupported: the record is valid but cookie has no way to drive it (for example an unknown protocol family or capabilities the endpoint cannot honor);
  • needs setup: provider setup values such as a region or resource name are missing;
  • needs credentials: no authored or stored credentials are available.

Where it shows:

  • Provider rows in /connect explain a connected or configured provider that yields no usable models, for example connected · no usable models: 4 quarantined (invalid_catalog_model_record). An unconfigured provider is flagged only when connecting could not help because every model is quarantined or unsupported.
  • Provider details (Enter on a row) count every kind, list each unavailable model of a configured provider with its reason, and show the models.dev documentation URL and environment variable names.
  • The model picker lists configured providers' unavailable models as a dimmed Unavailable (N) — not selectable group below the selectable models.
  • The connect form shows Docs: <url> and, for single-API-key providers, a config line such as [providers.kimi] source = "models_dev", api_key = "${env:KIMI_API_KEY}". cookie never reads those environment variables on its own; only the authored ${env:NAME} interpolation does.
  • The catalog line at the top of the /connect panel names the catalog source (network, cache, or bundled bootstrap), an age warning after 7 or 30 days, quarantine counts, and the last refresh error.
  • The CLI: cookie connect lists model counts per provider and prints the unavailable models, docs URL, and config alternative in the provider details. cookie run --model <provider/model> names the reason when that model is unavailable.

Per-model reasons are listed only for providers you configured (authored or stored); unconfigured providers report counts alone.

docs.title: Provider fields
docs.text:
Key Type Default Description source string (required) Must be "models_dev". base_url string (none) Override of the provider-level API URL; per-model catalog endpoints follow the rules above. Must be https, or http to localhost, 127.0.0.1, or ::1. Requires same-definition auth (api_key or auth_override) unless it is such a loopback URL, and never inherits provider-store setup or credentials. Forbidden for families that compute their endpoint from setup (Vertex, Bedrock, Azure). setup map of string values empty Setup fields the provider recipe requires (for example project, location, region, resource_name). Native Azure Responses compaction also requires model, version, and deployment_type. Interpolates ${env:NAME}. api_key string (none) Single-secret default auth. Allowed only for providers whose default method is an unambiguous single API key. Interpolates ${env:NAME}. auth_override table (none) Explicit auth method override. Mutually exclusive with api_key. cache table family default Prompt-cache policy matching the resolved adaptor family. headers map of strings empty Provider request-header overrides. models map empty Sparse per-model overrides: enabled, display_name, model_id, generation_options, adaptor_options, variants, default_variant, compaction, headers, pricing. Unmentioned catalog models remain available. Cannot invent models or directly change catalog capabilities.

Within a model override, compaction defaults to "unsupported". Set it to "openai-responses-compact" for the OpenAI Responses recipe or "azure-responses-compact" for the Azure Responses recipe. The compiler derives the native capability from this setting and rejects it for other recipes. The Azure provider identity must be azure.openai to match Oven's native scope. Frozen manifests store the compiled native/unsupported capability, not this setting string, so they never contain the retired "v1" value. Authored "v1" fails with a migration error naming the adapter-specific replacement.

auth_override:

Key Type Description method string One of the current auth method IDs (see below). values map of strings Credential values keyed by credential field name (for example api_key, access_token, access_key_id, secret_access_key, session_token). Interpolates ${env:NAME}.

docs.title: Managed model overrides
docs.text:
Use models.<model-id> for a sparse override, not an allowlist. Unmentioned models and omitted or empty variant maps retain catalog availability and variants. An unknown catalog model ID is an error; use a custom provider to define new models. Omitted enabled retains catalog behavior; false disables the model. Capabilities cannot be authored on a managed override.

This complete file illustrates an override for the bundled catalog's gpt-5 model. Confirm availability in your runtime before making requests:

[providers.openai]
source = "models_dev"
api_key = "${env:OPENAI_API_KEY}"

[providers.openai.models.gpt-5]
generation_options = { max_output_tokens = 8192 }
default_variant = "base"

[providers.openai.models.gpt-5.variants.high]
generation_options = { max_output_tokens = 4096 }

Model overrides accept enabled, display_name, model_id, generation_options, adaptor_options, pricing, variants, default_variant, compaction, and headers. Except for the explicit compaction policy described above, omitted fields retain catalog/base values. Display names and generation settings have the same constraints as custom definitions. Variant and pricing rules are below.

docs.title: Catalog reasoning variants
docs.text:
Managed models get variants from the catalog's reasoning_options:

  • Each effort level becomes a variant of the same name (low, high, max, ...).
  • A toggle becomes off and on; on is dropped when a supported effort or budget variant already turns reasoning on.
  • A token budget becomes budget-min (the catalog minimum), budget-high (half the usable maximum), and budget-max. The usable maximum is the catalog maximum capped at 31,999 tokens and at the output limit less 4,096 tokens kept for visible output (a 32K-output model's budget-max is 27,904). A dynamic minimum (-1) becomes budget-auto.

Variants the selected wire cannot express are dropped. Wire mapping by family:

Family Effort off on Budget Anthropic and Anthropic-compatible thinking = {type = "adaptive", display = "summarized"} plus output_config.effort thinking = {type = "disabled"} adaptive, summarized thinking = {type = "enabled", budget_tokens = N, display = "summarized"} Claude on Bedrock Converse additionalModelRequestFields thinking = {type = "adaptive", display = "summarized"} plus output_config.effort thinking = {type = "disabled"} adaptive, summarized thinking = {type = "enabled", budget_tokens = N} Other Bedrock Converse models reasoningConfig.maxReasoningEffort reasoningConfig.type = "disabled" reasoningConfig.type = "enabled" reasoningConfig.budgetTokens OpenAI-compatible Chat reasoning_effort provider switch below provider switch below not sent

Claude models before 4.6 accept only manual budgets, so their effort and on variants send an enabled budget of half the output room above those 4,096 visible tokens (1,024 to 16,000 tokens) instead of adaptive thinking. Claude on Bedrock follows the same rules and requires its signed thinking to be replayed, so its native replay is required.

The Anthropic wire sends max_tokens as visible output plus the thinking budget, and the total may not exceed the model's output limit. Requests send the full output limit (or a smaller agent cap) as visible output, so with a manual budget the visible output is lowered to output limit - budget when it would not otherwise fit; a smaller agent cap that fits is kept.

OpenAI-compatible providers get off/on only where the provider documents a thinking switch: thinking = {type = "disabled" | "enabled"} for DeepSeek, Z.ai/Zhipu GLM, and Volcengine Ark; enable_thinking = false | true for Alibaba Cloud Model Studio (alibaba, alibaba-cn); and reasoning_effort = "none" for Kimi Code, which has no on variant. Kimi Code serves thinking-off K3 requests with its K2.8 Preview model. Other providers, including Moonshot, get no toggle variants.

docs.title: Custom providers
docs.text: Custom providers are config-only, never appear in /connect, and never use the provider store. Any valid provider ID is allowed; on collision with a catalog provider ID the custom definition takes precedence.

docs.title: Custom model example
docs.text:
Complete config.toml for an illustrative endpoint. Replace the URL, model ID, limits, and capability declarations with those of your actual service. The reasoning-only variants inherit sampling and endpoint settings from the base:

[providers."custom.example"]
source = "custom"
endpoint = "https://api.example.invalid/v1"
adaptor = "openai-compatible"
auth = { method = "bearer-api-key-v1", values = { api_key = "${env:CUSTOM_API_KEY}" } }

[providers."custom.example".models."example-model"]
display_name = "Example Model"
model_id = "backend-model-v1"
generation_options = { temperature = 1.0, top_p = 0.95, max_output_tokens = 4096 }
adaptor_options = { request_endpoint = "completions" }

[providers."custom.example".models."example-model".capabilities]
input = ["text"]
output = ["text"]
context_tokens = 32768
output_tokens = 4096
reasoning = true
temperature = true
top_p = true
seed = false
media = {}

[providers."custom.example".models."example-model".variants.low]
reasoning = { type = "effort", value = "low" }

[providers."custom.example".models."example-model".variants.medium]
reasoning = { type = "effort", value = "medium" }

[providers."custom.example".models."example-model".variants.xhigh]
model_id = "backend-model-high-v1"
reasoning = { type = "effort", value = "xhigh" }

The local selection key is custom.example/example-model. The base, low, and medium variants send backend-model-v1; xhigh sends backend-model-high-v1. All variants still inherit the base sampling and endpoint settings unless overridden. No default variant is selected by this example. Setting an effort requests that behavior; parsing or HTTP acceptance does not prove that the backend implements distinct effort levels.

For a local service, change endpoint to its loopback base URL, such as http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1, and use auth = { method = "no-auth-v1", values = {} }. Compatible Responses supports tools and native replay with no auth when explicitly declared and supported by the server; it is not restricted to a tool-less text-only legacy path.

docs.title: Provider fields
docs.text: Key Type Default Description source string (required) Must be "custom". endpoint string (required) Absolute, query-free URL. Must be https, or http to localhost/a loopback address. Interpolates ${env:NAME}. adaptor string (required) Protocol adaptor ID (see below). setup map of string values empty Adaptor-required setup fields (Vertex location/project/resource, Bedrock region, Azure api_version/deployment). Interpolates ${env:NAME}. auth table (required) Typed auth definition (see below). headers map of strings empty Public provider request-header overrides. Supports environment and session templates. cache table adaptor default Prompt-cache policy matching adaptor. models map (required) At least one custom model definition.

docs.title: Authentication and adaptors
docs.text:
Custom auth accepts required method and values, plus optional parameters (empty by default). Each method requires exactly the listed credential fields; only api-key-header-v1 accepts parameters.

Method Credential fields in values Additional requirement no-auth-v1 Empty map No parameters bearer-api-key-v1 api_key Bearer header api-key-header-v1 api_key parameters = { header_name = "x-api-key" } or "api-key" anthropic-api-key-v1 api_key Anthropic key header google-api-key-header-v1 api_key Google key header oauth-access-token-v1 access_token Caller-supplied access token aws-sigv4-credentials-v1 access_key_id, secret_access_key, optional session_token SigV4 signing azure-api-key-v1 api_key Azure key header Custom adaptor Allowed auth methods Required setup openai-compatible Bearer, API-key-header, no-auth None openai-chat, openai-responses Bearer, no-auth None anthropic, anthropic-compatible Anthropic API key None google-gemini Google API key None google-vertex-gemini OAuth access token project, location; resource defaults to publishers/google aws-bedrock-converse AWS SigV4 region azure-openai-chat, azure-openai-responses Azure API key deployment, api_version cohere-v2-chat Bearer None

The short auth labels above refer to the full method IDs in the preceding table. Managed providers instead use their catalog family recipes, including their setup fields and allowed methods; /connect presents that exact form. Vertex, Bedrock, and Azure compute routes from setup and reject arbitrary managed base_url overrides. Custom endpoints must satisfy the selected adaptor's route constraints too.

docs.title: Model fields
docs.text:
Custom model definition under [providers."custom.x".models."<model-id>"]:

Key Type Default Description enabled boolean true Whether the model is compiled into the runtime. display_name string (required) Nonblank, at most 512 bytes, no control characters. model_id string inherited Provider request identifier, independent of the local selection key; see Request model identity. capabilities table (required) Explicit capability declarations (see below). generation_options table empty Generation settings (see below). adaptor_options table empty Typed adaptor-specific settings (see below). pricing table absent Whole-model rate override, including an explicitly empty rate set. headers map of strings empty Model request-header overrides. Variants accept the same header map. variants map empty Implicit variant creation or sparse overrides. default_variant string (none) "base" or a named variant that must exist in variants.

docs.title: Request model identity
docs.text:
Optional model_id is accepted on custom models, managed-model overrides, and variants. Later supplied values win:

  1. Provider-supplied identifier, normally the catalog/model key; custom Azure uses its configured setup.deployment as the fallback.
  2. Model-level model_id.
  3. Variant-level model_id.

Omission inherits. Values must be nonempty, at most 2,048 bytes, without control characters or surrounding whitespace, and valid for the selected adaptor's request route. Wire identifiers are not restricted to local alias syntax. OpenAI-style and Messages requests use the resolved model field; Gemini and Vertex use it in their model resource, Bedrock in its model path, and Azure in its deployment/model mapping. Resource restrictions still apply: for example, Gemini requires a bare model ID rather than a models/ prefix, slash, colon, query, fragment, or whitespace. Unsupported route/identifier combinations fail when constructing the executable model, rather than ignoring the override.

Changing model_id does not rename the local model, change its pricing lookup, modify catalog membership, or infer new capabilities. A managed alias must still name an existing catalog entry. The selected effective wire ID and endpoint are frozen with the executable settings, so reconstruction preserves them even when the current configuration or catalog changes.

docs.title: Capabilities and media
docs.text:
Custom fields are required unless a default or omission rule is stated below.

Key Type Description input array of strings Nonempty modalities: text, image, audio, pdf, video; subject to adaptor support. output array of strings Currently only ["text"] is supported. Structured JSON is text, not a separate modality. context_tokens integer Context window in tokens; must be greater than zero. input_tokens integer Optional input-token limit for providers that document one below the context window; must be greater than zero and at most context_tokens. Omitted, the input budget is the context window less min(output cap, 32000, context_tokens / 2). Compaction triggers against this budget. output_tokens integer Maximum output tokens; must be greater than zero and at most context_tokens. tool_calling boolean Defaults to true when not declared or inherited. A model with tool_calling = false is unsupported and never selectable. parallel_tool_calls boolean Defaults to true; requires tool_calling = true. structured_output boolean Defaults to true; declares JSON-structured output support. reasoning boolean Reasoning support. temperature boolean Temperature parameter support. top_p boolean Top-p parameter support. seed boolean Seed parameter support. compaction string Defaults to "unsupported", the only accepted custom capability value. Native opt-in is managed-model configuration. native_replay string Optional "unsupported", "optional", or "required"; omission derives supported replay from the resolved adaptor and endpoint. media map Per-kind (image, audio, pdf, video) input limits: nonempty mime_types string array, positive max_bytes and max_count. max_count is per request: when the history holds more parts of a kind, the oldest are replaced by a text placeholder in the outgoing request (see media reads). Exactly the non-text input modalities need entries; text-only models use {}.

The three optimistic true defaults are declarations, not endpoint detection. Set unsupported features to false. Invalid effective declarations are errors. For an endpoint without parallel tool calls or structured output, add this fragment to its capabilities table:

parallel_tool_calls = false
structured_output = false

cookie-agent requires tool calling. tool_calling = false (which also requires parallel_tool_calls = false) is accepted, but the model compiles as unsupported with the reason no tool calling and is never offered for selection; a fallback chain skips it like any other unavailable model.

These flags neither request JSON for ordinary turns nor guarantee parallel execution or backend support. Managed models retain explicit catalog false declarations; only missing metadata falls back to true.

Input support also depends on the delivery channel. A modality accepted in a user turn is not necessarily accepted in a tool result. Counts are enforced per request; a tool result and its emitted messages share a combined budget. See media reads for supported channels, MIME types, retention, and operational limits. Unsupported combinations produce tool errors, not generated media output.

docs.title: Replay and cancellation
docs.text:
Cancellation is derived as local-only; it does not guarantee server generation or billing stops, and capabilities.cancellation is rejected.

All integrated SDK codecs support replay. Automatic replay is optional except Anthropic reasoning, which requires native state. Azure ordinary replay does not require deployment revision metadata; model, version, and deployment_type remain required for native compaction. Azure Chat supports native text/tool replay, not provider-authoritative reasoning replay. Explicit replay declarations remain authoritative and fail when incompatible; native_replay = "unsupported" disables replay. Automatic replay is recomputed for the effective variant endpoint.

Replay preserves assistant response history, not a prior HTTP request. With replay enabled, the target prefers valid native blocks it supports:

Content Eligibility Standard supported text, tools, and non-encrypted reasoning blocks Portable across local models, variants, providers, endpoints, headers, and deployment fingerprints when the target supports their format and semantics Encrypted/opaque reasoning: Responses encrypted_content, redacted Messages/Converse state, Gemini/Vertex thoughtSignature Target format support and equal, known source/target effective wire model IDs are both required Custom-adaptor-specific or unknown blocks/codecs Only explicit target support authorizes replay; unknown formats are not guessed or translated

Signed visible thinking is not encrypted reasoning. A supported Messages signed thinking block can remain eligible across wire-model changes, but is not automatically convertible to Responses reasoning. Native payload integrity and agreement with normalized history are still validated; provider/header/model fingerprints are not additional eligibility restrictions for standard blocks. When a validated bundle can be separated safely, portable siblings survive exclusion of an ineligible encrypted block.

Ordinary tool history can reconstruct from normalized text and calls if native data is unavailable. Required continuation state cannot silently disappear: missing, corrupt, or ineligible required reasoning/signatures fail closed, even when ordinary siblings are portable. Saved evidence that opaque state was required is distinct from an ordinary integrity marker; a tool call alone does not imply encrypted state. Legacy history without that evidence is read best-effort, not repaired by inventing missing native data. Missing source wire identity never establishes equality for encrypted replay.

Switching providers can send eligible prior native state to the new endpoint. Equal wire model IDs are necessary for encrypted replay, but a different service can still reject ciphertext or signatures, even for that ID. A provider HTTP 400 is not automatically recovered by stripping reasoning and resending. Errors follow the normal retry and fallback policy. Replay neither enables prompt caching nor guarantees cache hits or live backend acceptance. Cache policy and native compaction retain their separate scope and validation rules.

docs.title: Generation options
docs.text:
Model and variant generation_options supply shared generation settings. On a custom base model, omission leaves optional values unset and stop empty; on managed models and variants, supplied fields override individually. Agent limits and explicit request settings can further constrain the effective request.

Key Type Description temperature float Finite value; requires capabilities.temperature. top_p float Finite value; requires capabilities.top_p. max_output_tokens integer Must be greater than zero and at most capabilities.output_tokens. Sent when the agent sets no output cap of its own; without it, requests send the full output_tokens. Catalog models have no default. stop array of strings Stop sequences. seed integer Requires capabilities.seed. tool_choice string or table "auto", "none", "required", or { named = "tool-name" }; requires capabilities.tool_calling.

Current integration limitation: authored stop, seed, and tool_choice are accepted, validated, inherited, and recorded in run bindings, but the shared request-default application does not forward them to SDK requests. Do not rely on those authored fields to control a live request. Temperature, top-p, maximum output tokens, and supported reasoning settings do reach request construction; final behavior still depends on the selected adaptor and backend.

docs.title: Adaptor options
docs.text:
These are typed model/variant settings, not arbitrary JSON body fields. All are optional; omission inherits before adaptor defaults apply. Explicit false and empty lists remain overrides. Nonempty wrong-adaptor settings fail.

Key Type Description request_endpoint string "completions" (Chat Completions) or "responses"; selects the complete codec and route. beta array of strings Anthropic beta header values; rejected for non-Anthropic adaptors. organization string OpenAI-Organization header for OpenAI Chat (with or without auth) and authenticated OpenAI Responses; rejected for compatible and unauthenticated Responses. project string OpenAI-Project header for OpenAI Chat (with or without auth) and authenticated OpenAI Responses; rejected for compatible and unauthenticated Responses. store boolean OpenAI/compatible Responses only, not Azure. The stateless encoder supports false; true is rejected.

docs.title: Request endpoint
docs.text:
Adaptor Omitted completions responses openai-chat Chat Completions Supported Supported openai-responses Responses Supported Supported openai-compatible Chat Completions Supported Compatible Responses azure-openai-chat Azure Chat Supported Supported azure-openai-responses Azure Responses Supported Supported Anthropic, Gemini, Vertex Gemini, Bedrock Converse, Cohere Native API Rejected Rejected

Managed omission preserves catalog routing. Selection chooses the encoder, decoder, streaming protocol, and route, not just a URL suffix. completions means /chat/completions, not the legacy /completions API. Azure retains its deployment-specific routing. Backend compatibility must be verified separately; selecting Responses cannot add it to a server that only implements Chat.

Changing a variant endpoint validates all inherited settings against that endpoint. For example, an inherited store = false conflicts with a Chat variant; omit it on the base and put it only on the Responses variant instead.

docs.title: Variants and inheritance
docs.text:
Variant entries create absent IDs and sparsely update existing catalog variants. Generation and adaptor fields inherit in order: catalog base, model overrides, catalog variant, user variant. Omitted fields inherit, explicit false survives, and lists replace ([] clears). Reasoning omission preserves the prior value; a supplied tagged reasoning object replaces it as a whole. Headers merge by normalized name, preserving empty-string deletion markers through composition.

Variants accept display_name, model_id, generation_options, adaptor_options, reasoning, headers, and optional enabled. enabled = false removes an existing variant or is a no-op for an absent ID; other fields alongside it are errors. Existing positions are preserved, and new IDs append in sorted order. An omitted or empty map preserves catalog variants. Named defaults must exist and be enabled after composition. A new unnamed display label is derived from its ID. Custom variants have no catalog layer, so editing shared base settings changes every variant that does not override those fields.

default_variant selects a variant; it is not a generation setting. Omission does not select the first authored variant. "base" explicitly selects the base; named defaults are resolved after creation, overrides, and disabling.

Reasoning is optional and requires the model's reasoning capability. The tagged object accepts exactly one of:

Type Fields Constraints effort value none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max, default; not Cohere toggle enabled boolean Anthropic, Gemini, Vertex Gemini, Bedrock Converse, Cohere budget_tokens value signed integer Same families as toggle; final adaptor validation determines supported budgets

A concrete off toggle or none effort is not removal of the reasoning object. There is no null/clear operation. Example fragment disabling a managed variant:

[providers.openai.models.gpt-5.variants.low]
enabled = false

docs.title: Provider definitions and headers
docs.text: Providers are defined only in the user config.toml. The sparse rules above apply inside one provider definition. Headers use the separate Request Header composition and ownership rules; their values are public metadata, not secret-typed storage.

docs.title: Breaking configuration migration
docs.text: Removed keys fail without aliases: model_overrides becomes models, model and variant defaults becomes generation_options, and options becomes adaptor_options. Replace shape and the ineffective api_path with adaptor_options.request_endpoint. Remove authored capabilities.cancellation. Replace variant operation directives with sparse entries or enabled = false. Move top-level pricing to the model's pricing table.

docs.title: Prompt caching
docs.text:
Prompt-cache policy belongs to the provider definition. Omit cache to use the family defaults. A cache table is validated against the provider's resolved adaptor; wrong-family fields and unknown keys are load errors.

The following are fragments for already-defined providers, not a complete file:

[providers.anthropic.cache]
system = "1h"
tools = "1h"
rolling = "5m"

[providers."custom.bedrock".cache]
system = "5m"
tools = "5m"
rolling = "5m"

[providers.openai.cache]
mode = "auto"
ttl = "30m"
system = true
rolling = true

[providers."custom.compatible".cache]
prompt_cache_key = "tenant-${session_id}"

Here custom.bedrock is an existing custom aws-bedrock-converse provider. A managed provider can contain models routed through different adaptor families; a shared cache table must validate for its resolved models. In particular, do not apply a Converse-only cache policy to a mixed Bedrock catalog provider that also routes models through Responses. Use a custom provider for explicit family-specific policy when the managed definition cannot share it.

Anthropic defaults to system = "1h", tools = "1h", and rolling = "5m". system and tools accept "1h", "5m", or "off"; rolling accepts "5m" or "off". Marker order is tools, system, then rolling history, and a one-hour marker cannot follow a five-minute marker. Explicit "1h" placement requires the model's authored Anthropic beta options to contain extended-cache-ttl-2025-04-11; Cookie agent never inserts an anthropic-beta value on the user's behalf.

Bedrock has the same three fields and ordering rule. All three default to "5m"; setting all three to "off" emits no cache points. Rolling always marks the last non-system message. There is no enabled switch and no indexed messages list. System and tool points are omitted from requests without eligible system text or tools. The three structural placements stay below Bedrock's four-point request limit.

Anthropic and Bedrock use structural markers. The selected policy is frozen for the run, prior markers are cleared, and ordinary and compaction requests resolve the same system, tools, and last-non-system placements. Compaction shares the parent's cached prefix instead of creating an isolated cache namespace.

OpenAI and Azure OpenAI always send the session's bare UUIDv7 as prompt_cache_key; this has no configuration field or opt-out. Their cache table accepts prompt_cache_retention, mode, ttl, system, and rolling. prompt_cache_retention is "in_memory" or "24h". Setting mode or ttl, or setting system or rolling to true, enables GPT-5.6 controls. Both placements default to false; omitted mode and ttl then default to "auto" and "30m". The only accepted ttl is "30m". mode = "explicit" disables the provider-managed breakpoint, so system = false and rolling = false produce zero cache writes. There is no tools placement.

Custom openai-compatible providers accept only prompt_cache_key. Omission defaults to ${session_id}, an empty string disables the key, and another value is sent verbatim after ${session_id} expansion. The expanded value must be at most 64 characters. Other template variables are rejected.

Gemini caching is always implicit and has no configuration surface. A cache table on Google Gemini or Vertex Gemini providers is an error. Cohere caching is server-side automatic and likewise has no authored cache table.

Provider behavior changes independently of Cookie agent. See the official OpenAI prompt-caching guide, Gemini context-caching guide, Amazon Bedrock prompt-caching guide, Cohere API reference, and Anthropic prompt-caching guide for current model support, thresholds, retention, and billing.

docs.title: Breaking changes
docs.text:
1. The global [prompt_caching] table and all [prompt_caching.<family>] subtables are removed; use [providers.<id>.cache].
  2. Anthropic and Bedrock TTLs accept only "1h", "5m", and "off". The former "one_hour" and "five_minutes" values are removed. Configuration is strict: any other TTL string (for example "automatic", "short", "long", "standard", "none", or "ephemeral") was never a cookie-agent literal and is a hard error, not an alias.
  3. Google cache configuration is removed, including mode ("implicit", "explicit", or "off") and cached_content; Gemini caching is always implicit.
  4. Bedrock now uses only system, tools, and rolling. The enabled field, messages list, and each message entry's history_index and ttl fields are removed.
  5. First-party OpenAI and Azure cache tables no longer accept prompt_cache_key; the bare session UUIDv7 is always sent. OpenAI-compatible providers own that field, default to ${session_id}, and use prompt_cache_key = "" to disable it.
  6. OpenAI cache mode = "implicit" is removed; use mode = "auto". mode = "explicit" remains supported.

docs.title: Model pricing
docs.text:
Pricing overrides are empty by default. Managed models use prices from the selected models.dev catalog. Add an entry for a custom model absent from the catalog, or to override catalog prices with the provider terms that apply to your account. Catalog context tiers are selected independently for each request from its reported input-token count. Both managed and custom models use this model-local table. Rates are validated even for disabled or unavailable models; managed model IDs must still exist in the catalog.

[providers."custom.example".models."model-name".pricing]
input_per_million_usd = "1.25"
output_per_million_usd = "5.0"

All fields are optional quoted, finite, nonnegative decimal USD rates per million tokens. Quoting preserves the authored decimal exactly.

Rates use fixed-point precision of 12 decimal places in USD per million tokens, stored as an unsigned 128-bit scaled integer. Scientific notation is accepted when exactly representable. Negative values, non-finite values, overflow, and nonzero precision below that scale are rejected, not rounded. Pricing has no variant override. The example above is a fragment for an existing model.

Key Applies to input_per_million_usd Input tokens not attributed to cache reads or writes output_per_million_usd Plain, non-reasoning output tokens reasoning_per_million_usd Reasoning output tokens; falls back to the output rate when omitted cache_read_per_million_usd Provider-reported cache-read input tokens cache_write_per_million_usd Provider-reported cache-write input tokens

Precedence is config override, then catalog price, then no estimate. A config entry replaces the catalog rate set for that model. When a selected rate set does not distinguish cache reads or writes, those tokens use its plain input rate; reasoning tokens similarly use its output rate when no reasoning rate is present. An estimate is returned only when the selected source prices every nonzero observed category and the provider reports every split needed by a distinct rate. A session, agent, or global total is unpriced if any model within it is unpriced. These are estimates from provider-reported token counts, not invoices.

docs.title: Skill
docs.text: Skills are reusable instruction bundles loaded once when the runtime that contributes them starts. A skill is a directory whose name contains lowercase letters, digits, and single hyphens, with an exact-case SKILL.md file inside it. Other files under the directory are available as scripts, references, or assets.

docs.title: Discovery and precedence
docs.text:
A session's skills come from the runtimes it is attached to. The global runtime contributes the user skills:

  • ~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md (cross-client convention, shared with other agents)
  • ~/.cookie-agent/skills/<name>/SKILL.md (cookie-agent-native user skills, which win over the shared location)

Each coding runtime contributes the project skills it finds for its own workspace: .agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md, then .cookie-agent/skills/<name>/SKILL.md, in every directory from the repository root (the nearest ancestor with .git) down to the workspace, deeper directories winning. The built-in local runtime does this for the daemon's working directory when the daemon starts; another coding runtime does it when its instance starts.

The user locations resolve from the standard home directory and are the normal place for reusable personal skills; ~/.agents/skills is the right home for skills shared with other agents that follow the cross-client convention.

Same-named skills are replaced whole, never merged: a project skill shadows a user skill of the same name, and within one directory scope the cookie-agent-native root wins over .agents/skills. When project skills of two attachments share a name, each is offered as <attachment>_<name>, for example local_web_deploy and labpc_api_deploy, like colliding tools. Shadowed skills remain visible in skills.list, but cannot be invoked and are not offered by the TUI. A session without the global runtime has no user skills, and one without a coding runtime has no project skills. Skill files are not hot-reloaded; restart the engine after changing them.

docs.title: Authoring
docs.text:
Complete release-check/SKILL.md:

---
name: release-check
description: Check a release candidate for packaging and changelog problems.
when_to_use: Use before publishing a tagged build.
allowed-tools: Bash(git:*) Bash(jq:*) Read
argument-hint: <tag>
---
Review release $1 from $ARGUMENTS.
Read supporting files from ${COOKIE_SKILL_DIR}.

name and description are required; descriptions are limited to 1024 bytes. Optional fields are when_to_use, allowed-tools, disable-model-invocation, user-invocable, model, context, argument-hint, license, compatibility, and metadata. Unknown fields are errors. model must be a valid provider/model key and is rejected during discovery otherwise. context accepts only fork.

disable-model-invocation defaults to false and user-invocable defaults to true. allowed-tools is omitted by default (no extra grants); an authored empty string is invalid. Optional text fields are strings; model and context are unset by default, and metadata is an empty map of YAML values. Files are limited to 256 KiB and must have a nonempty body. The declared name must match the directory name.

Arguments replace $ARGUMENTS and positional $1, $2, and later forms. ${COOKIE_SKILL_DIR} expands to the skill directory. Expansion is textual and does not execute a shell.

docs.title: Invocation and permissions
docs.text:
The model uses skill({"name":"release-check","args":"v1.2.0"}). The tool is absent when policy leaves no skill effectively usable, and skills with disable-model-invocation: true are omitted from the model listing. In the TUI, users choose /skills in the command palette, search for a user-invocable skill, press Enter, and type optional arguments such as v1.2.0 into the prompt that follows. The highlighted skill's source, permission effect, and location show under the list. Headless runs use cookie run --skill release-check --skill-args v1.2.0 "Check the release".

Skill access uses the skill permission action and the skill name as its resource. A denied skill is hidden from the model listing. Headless runs can grant one skill with --allowed-tools skill:release-check.

allowed-tools uses the agentskills.io/Claude Code syntax: a space-separated string of bare Tool names or Tool(pattern) entries. Patterns may contain spaces and parentheses; a bare tool means *. Tool names are case-insensitive, and Edit maps to the write permission just like the builtin edit tool. Every other name is the permission action itself, lowercased: Read, Bash, Webfetch, and so on for the built-in tools, or a runtime's own action such as Browse(https://docs.rs/*). A name that lowercases to no valid action (see permissions) is an error. The older Cookie Agent action:pattern list form is not accepted.

A plugin's tools are granted by the actions their plugin declares, like a runtime's: Issue_read grants every issue_read call, and Issue_read(42) only the calls on resource 42.

Claude's prefix:* convention is translated to Cookie Agent's full-resource glob semantics. For example, Bash(git:*) creates grants for both git and git *, matching git, git status, and longer git commands. Other inner patterns pass through unchanged: Write(src/**) grants the src/** glob.

On load, these entries create turn-scoped allow grants labeled for that skill. A project skill's grants apply only to the tools of the attachment that contributed it (and, for Skill and Delegate grants, to the base layer's skill and delegate_subagent tools); a user skill's grants apply to every runtime. Grants from every skill loaded during the same turn are merged; loading a grantless skill does not remove grants from an earlier skill. The complete collection disappears on the next committed user input. Grants can only upgrade an ask decision to allow: they never override a deny, including the unmatched default deny, and they do not make a tool visible on their own. The agent still needs an explicit allow or ask rule for each granted action — for example bash: ask before relying on a skill's Bash grants. A model override applies to the next model turn only.

Every first rendered load appends skill_loaded, including the rendered body, source and base paths, arguments, and up to ten supporting-file paths. Loading the identical rendered body again appends skill_invocation_noted. Loaded skill bodies remain in model context across compaction. With context: fork, the exact staged skill payload is persisted in delegation admission. The child gets the rendered instructions once through its skill_loaded event and a synthetic user prompt starts the run. Forks use the normal delegation approval, queue, paging, cancellation, recovery, and permission behavior.

docs.title: Rust API Documentation
docs.text:
The workspace rustdoc output is published with each documentation version.

Open workspace API documentation

The API index includes all eleven workspace crates and documents public items only. Build it locally together with this site by running:

./scripts/build-docs.sh

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: The client protocol, the plugin protocol, the runtime protocol, and session history carry a compatibility promise: a client, plugin, or runtime written against 1.x keeps working with every daemon that speaks 1.x, and a session log keeps opening in every later build. These are the rules every change to them follows. The compatibility specification gives the reasons; this page states the rules.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text:
• Each protocol has a semver version MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH in crates/protocol/src/semver.rs: CLIENT_PROTOCOL_VERSION, PLUGIN_PROTOCOL_VERSION, and RUNTIME_PROTOCOL_VERSION. All three froze at 1.0.0.
  • Bump the major for a breaking change: something removed or renamed, a meaning changed, a new required member in a message the peer receives, a closed enum grown. Peers of different majors never connect, and a daemon does not keep serving the previous major.
  • Bump the minor for any addition: a method, a notification, a hook, an event type, a display-block kind, an optional member, a value of an open enum.
  • Bump the patch for a change that leaves every wire shape alone: a documented behaviour clarified, a validation bug fixed.
  • Know which surfaces a message belongs to. Session events belong to the client and the plugin protocols, so adding an event type bumps both minors. The tool/* messages belong to the plugin and the runtime protocols. Display blocks belong to all three.
  • Update the human-readable references in the same commit as a bump: AGENTS.md lists them.

docs.title: Handshakes
docs.text:
• Read the peer's protocol_version from the raw JSON before decoding anything else (negotiate_version), and answer another major with unsupported_protocol naming both versions.
  • Two peers of one major share the lower of their minors. Send a command (a method, a member of a command's params, a hook) only when the receiver's minor includes it. Information an older receiver ignores may stay in place; a value an older receiver would misread may not.
  • Features carry only what depends on configuration, never what a version implies. A receiver ignores a feature it does not know.

docs.title: Decoding
docs.text:
What arrives Unknown member Unknown enum value or tag Information (results, notifications, events, hook params, initialize results, stored events) Ignored The documented fallback Command (client params, producer/*, tool/progress, tool/detachable, plugin/emit) Refused: -32602 unknown_field with its JSON path Refused: -32602 unknown_variant with its JSON path
  • Never put #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] on a type that crosses a surface as information. The checker rejects an information type whose schema has additionalProperties: false. Command params stay strict, and so does configuration.
  • Writers stay strict. Validate every value before it is sent or written: bounds, required members, grammar. Strictness lives in constructors and in the writer's validation step, not in the decoder.
  • Make every enum a reader may meet open, and document what its unknown value means where it is read: Open<T> (open_enum!) for tagged enums with data, an Unknown variant or a #[serde(other)] fallback for unit enums, validated label strings for label-like values. Mark open enums x-open: true in the schema. Close an enum only when growing it is a breaking change by design, and say so.
  • A known tag with a malformed body is an error, not Unknown: Unknown means "from a newer peer".
  • Do not add #[non_exhaustive] to protocol types; only the plugin SDK's own types use it.

docs.title: Wire types
docs.text:
• No surface embeds a type owned by oven-sdk or by engine policy, stored events included. Where the engine needs data it does not model, store an opaque value and decode it best-effort when it is used, never when loading.
  • Every error is a registry error (cookie_agent_protocol::errors): a stable data.code, a message a user understands, an optional hint, and detail for technical detail. Add a code to the registry rather than building error data by hand; clients branch only on data.code.

docs.title: Making a wire change
docs.text:
1. Change the type or the method registry (surface_methods in crates/protocol/src/bindings.rs).
  2. Bump each affected surface's version by what the change needs (above).
  3. Run crates/protocol/scripts/update-compat-baseline.sh. It regenerates crates/protocol/compat/<surface>/ and refuses when a version lacks the bump its changes require.
  4. Run crates/protocol/scripts/check-schema-additive.sh, which CI runs: it compares the generated schemas with the baselines under the rules of the specification's section 7.1 and runs the checker's mutation test.
  5. Commit the baselines with the change and the reference updates.

A change the checker calls breaking needs a major bump; there is no way to mark a breaking change as compatible.

docs.title: Test sets
docs.text:
• Frozen corpora are never regenerated. crates/protocol/compat/corpus/ holds, per surface and version, recorded conversations that the current build must keep accepting, and future fixtures that inject what a newer build could send. crates/engine/tests/fixtures/history/<format>/ holds recorded session trees with snapshots of their projection and model history. No COOKIE_UPDATE_* switch applies to them, and the baseline update leaves them alone.
  • When a test over frozen data fails, fix the code, not the data. A failure means the change breaks data an earlier build wrote or sent.
  • A minor release that adds wire shapes records its own corpus directory next to the earlier ones. A history format bump records history/<format>/ with its own recorder run, beside the older formats, which keep testing their converters.

docs.title: Session history
docs.text:
• Class every event as state (anything the projection, model history, delegation recovery, goals, producers, approvals, or usage read) or audit (everything else), and list its class in Events. Audit events carry "skippable": true; a reader skips an unknown skippable event and opens a log with an unknown state event render-only.
  • Additive rules for writers: a new optional member must be safe to ignore, its absence meaning the old behaviour; a member whose absence would be misread needs a new event type; a new open-enum value needs a fallback that is safe for old readers.
  • The loader never recomputes what it can read. Trust stored fingerprints, quarantine a record that fails a cross-event check instead of failing the open, keep size caps writer-only, and keep every record's raw line so that a fork, a publish, or a conversion copies what this build did not understand.
  • Storage encodings stay on disk. An encoding only the log holds, such as a tool result's display ranges of its output, is expanded when the log is read; nothing outside the engine meets it.
  • The history format bumps only for a change that cannot follow the additive rules, and every bump ships a converter: crates/engine/src/events/convert/v<N>_to_v<N+1>.rs, a pure function over the old log's JSON lines that never uses old Rust types, registered in CONVERTERS and kept forever, so converters chain. Converters are the only migrations allowed; nothing else upconverts, aliases, or migrates stored or authored data. See History formats.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Configuration is not a compatibility surface. It stays strict: unknown keys, removed fields, wrong types, and malformed values are hard errors, and authored files are never migrated or upconverted. A configuration key change is a configuration change, not a protocol change, even where config.get and config.apply carry the document.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Every error the client, plugin, and runtime protocols send has a stable data.code and a message a user can understand; data.hint says what to do next where that helps, and data.detail carries technical detail for a details view. Clients branch only on data.code, show message and then hint, and show detail on request. A code a client does not know is still readable: its message and hint are written for people. See the compatibility spec section 6.

The JSON-RPC code is -32000 for every application error; the protocol codes are the standard -32700, -32600, -32601, -32602, and -32603, and -32001 (handshake required), -32002 (unsupported_protocol), and -32003 (unauthenticated).

data.code JSON-RPC Meaning Message Hint Fields parse_error -32700 A frame that is not JSON; the daemon answers it and reads on, while the shared client closes its connection. A message could not be read because it is not valid JSON. – – invalid_request -32600 A frame that is not a JSON-RPC request, notification, or reply. A message is not a valid request. – – request_id_required -32600 A method that only works as a request arrived as a notification. {method} must be sent as a request with an ID. – method: The method that was sent as a notification. method_not_found -32601 A method the receiver does not know. The other side does not know the method {method}. Update the older of the two programs. method: The method name. invalid_params -32602 Params that do not match the method. The request's parameters are not valid. – field (optional): The JSON path of the first bad member. unknown_field -32602 A command carried a member its receiver does not know. The request has a member the receiver does not know: {field}. Update the older of the two programs. field: The JSON path of the member. unknown_variant -32602 A command carried an enum value or tag its receiver does not know. The request uses a value the receiver does not know at {field}. Update the older of the two programs. field: The JSON path of the value.value (optional): The value that is not known. internal_error -32603 A failure the receiver cannot describe further. Something went wrong while handling the request. Try again; if it keeps failing, check the daemon log. – handshake_required -32001 A request before the handshake. The connection must complete its handshake first. – – unsupported_protocol -32002 The peer speaks another major version of the protocol. The two sides speak incompatible protocol versions: {supported_version} here and {peer_version} on the other side. Update cookie or the program connecting to it so that their versions match. supported_version: The version the receiver speaks.peer_version: The version the peer sent. unauthenticated -32003 A request before authentication, or a wrong token. The connection is not authenticated. Connect with the daemon's token. – engine_error -32000 A failure with no more specific code; detail says what failed. The daemon could not complete the request. See the details for the cause. – no_runnable_model -32000 No configured model can run: no provider is connected or none offers the model. No model is ready to run. Connect a provider with /connect, or choose another model. – provider_store_reload_failed -32000 Reloading the provider store after a change failed. The saved provider connections could not be reloaded. Check the details, then reconnect the provider. – session_owned_elsewhere -32000 Another process holds the session's lock. This session is open in another cookie process. Close it there, or open it read-only. session_id (optional): The session. session_not_found -32000 A request named a session the daemon does not have. The session does not exist. – session_id (optional): The session. session_running -32000 run.start on a session that is running. Another run is already active in this session. Steer or queue the input instead, or wait for the run to finish. session_id: The session.client_run_id (optional): The run request's idempotency key. idempotency_conflict -32000 An idempotency key was reused with different params. This request reuses the ID of an earlier request that was different. Send the request again with a new ID. session_id (optional): The session the request named.provider_id (optional): The provider the request named.approval_id (optional): The approval the request named.client_run_id (optional): The reused run key.client_rename_id (optional): The reused rename key.client_response_id (optional): The reused approval-response key.client_connect_id (optional): The reused connect key.client_request_id (optional): The reused request key. stale_revert -32000 A revert named an expected last event that is no longer the last. The session changed before the revert could be applied. Reload the session and choose the point to revert to again. session_id: The session.current_last_seq: The session's last event now. not_a_root_session -32000 session.delete named a delegated session instead of a root. This session is a subagent of another session, and only a whole session tree can be deleted. Delete its root session, which deletes its subagents with it. session_id: The session.root_session_id: The root of its tree. session_tree_running -32000 session.delete on a tree with an active run, a compaction, or a subagent waiting for a slot. This session or one of its subagents is running, so it cannot be deleted. Wait for it to finish, or cancel it, then delete the session. session_id: The root session.running_session_id (optional): The session of the tree that is busy. session_changed -32000 session.delete named an expected last event that is no longer the root's last. The session has new activity since it was shown, so it was not deleted. Review the new turns, then delete the session again if you still want to. session_id: The session.current_last_seq: The session's last event now. session_requires_newer_engine -32000 The session's log has an event or history format this build cannot continue. This session was written by a newer version of cookie, so it can only be viewed. Update cookie to continue this session. session_id (optional): The session.event (optional): The event type this build does not know.history_format (optional): The session's history format. sequence_broken -32000 The session's log has a record whose sequence does not advance; the readable part opens render-only. This session's log is damaged after event {seq}, so it can only be viewed. Fork the session from an earlier point to continue it. session_id (optional): The session.seq: The first record whose sequence does not advance. unreadable_model_binding -32000 An operation needed a run's stored model binding, which this build cannot decode. The stored setup of the model {model} cannot be read by this version of cookie. Start a new run, which resolves the model again. model: The model whose stored binding cannot be read. agent_unavailable -32000 An agent that is disabled, not eligible in this session, unknown, or whose model is unavailable. The selected agent cannot run here. Choose another agent or model; the details say why. agent (optional): The agent. run_not_found -32000 A request named a run that is not active. The run does not exist or has already finished. – run_id (optional): The run. invalid_title -32000 A rename with an empty, too long, or unsafe title. The title is not valid. Use a shorter title without control characters. session_id: The session. tree_usage_session_missing -32000 session.tree_usage met a session that is gone. A session of this tree no longer exists, so its usage cannot be added up. – session_id (optional): The missing session. tree_usage_delegation_corrupt -32000 session.tree_usage met a delegation record that does not decode. A subagent record of this tree is damaged, so its usage cannot be added up. – invocation_id (optional): The damaged delegation. goal_rejected -32000 A goal operation the session's goal state does not allow. The goal could not be changed: {reason}. – reason: Why, in the daemon's words. producer_rejected -32000 A producer operation was refused: messaging is not open, the session is not attached, or the operation failed. The message source's request was refused. See the details for why. – plugin_rejected -32000 A plugin hook or request refused the operation. A plugin refused the request: {reason}. – reason: Why, in the plugin's or the daemon's words.plugin (optional): The plugin. plugin_hook_failed -32000 A hook of a plugin that blocks on failure timed out, was not connected, or answered with an error or a malformed result. The plugin {plugin} could not check this request in its {hook} hook, and it refuses what it cannot check. Check the plugin's status in /plugins, restart or fix it, and try again. plugin: The plugin.hook: The hook that failed, such as user_before_input. runtime_rejected -32000 A runtime could not be attached, detached, started, or reached. The runtime request was refused: {reason}. – reason: Why, in the daemon's words. mcp_rejected -32000 An mcp.server.* or mcp.auth.* request the daemon could not carry out. The MCP server request was refused: {reason}. – reason: Why, in the daemon's words. machine_not_found -32000 A machines.* request named a machine the registry does not have. There is no machine named {machine}. See machines.list for the machines. machine: The machine name. machine_name_taken -32000 machines.rename to the name of another machine, or of a memory folder that belongs to none. The machine name {name} is taken. Choose another name, or merge the two machines. name: The machine name. machine_in_use -32000 machines.forget of a machine with connected runtimes or a nonempty memory folder. The machine {machine} still has connected runtimes or memories. Disconnect its runtimes and move or delete its memories first, or merge it into another machine. machine: The machine name. machine_memory_conflict -32000 machines.merge of two machines whose memory folders share a file name; nothing changed. Both {from} and {into} have a memory file named {name}. Rename or delete one of them, then merge again. from: The machine merged.into: The machine merged into.name: A file both memory folders have. machine_merge_self -32000 machines.merge with the same machine as from and into. The machine {machine} cannot be merged into itself. – machine: The machine name. runtime_not_pinned -32000 machines.unassign of a runtime ID no machine pins. The runtime {runtime} is not pinned to a machine. – runtime: The runtime ID. machine_store_failed -32000 Reading or writing machines.json, taking the memory lock, or moving a memory folder failed; nothing changed. The machine registry or a machine's memory folder could not be changed. See the details, then check that the cookie data directory is writable. – memory_url_invalid -32000 A memory.* request named something that is not a memory URL. That is not a memory URL: {reason}. Memory URLs are user://, agent://, machine:///, and project:///, in lowercase. url: The URL as sent.reason: Why it is not a memory URL. memory_not_found -32000 memory.read or memory.delete of a memory that does not exist, or a memory.write with a revision for one that does not. There is no memory at {url}. See memory.list for the memories. url: The memory URL. memory_exists -32000 memory.write without a revision for a memory that exists; nothing changed. The memory {url} already exists. Read it and send its revision to replace it. url: The memory URL.revision: The memory's current revision. memory_revision_mismatch -32000 memory.write or memory.delete with a revision other than the file's current one; nothing changed. The memory {url} changed since it was read. Read it again, then repeat the change on the current text. url: The memory URL.revision: The memory's current revision. memory_invalid -32000 memory.write text that does not parse, breaks a rule of the file format, or is longer than [memory] max_file_bytes; nothing changed. The text is not a valid memory: {reason}. A memory starts with frontmatter that holds a one-line description and optional keywords, then its Markdown body. url: The memory URL.reason: What is wrong with the text. memory_refused -32000 A memory.* change the memory rules do not allow, such as creating an agent:// memory for an agent the agent registry does not have. The memory change was refused: {reason}. – url: The memory URL.reason: Why, in the daemon's words. memory_busy -32000 The memory lock could not be taken in time; nothing changed. Another cookie process is changing memory. Try again in a moment. – memory_store_failed -32000 Reading or writing a file in the memory folder failed. The memory folder could not be read or changed. See the details, then check that the cookie data directory is readable and writable. – config_apply_refused -32000 config.apply changed nothing; detail says why. The configuration was not changed ({reason}). On a conflict, reload the configuration and apply the change again; otherwise fix what the details name. reason: conflict, invalid_configuration, or invalid_change. approval_not_found -32000 A response named an approval the session does not have. The approval request does not exist. – approval_id: The approval. approval_not_pending -32000 A response to an approval that is no longer pending. The approval request was already answered or cancelled. – approval_id: The approval. approval_revision_conflict -32000 A response to an outdated revision of an approval. The approval request changed before the answer arrived. Review the request again and answer it. approval_id: The approval.expected_revision (optional): The revision the response answered.found_revision (optional): The approval's revision now. decision_not_allowed -32000 A response with a decision the approval does not offer.
