Parsing must preserve omission versus explicit empty values. In particular, stop and beta currently use vectors whose deserialization defaults can erase this distinction. Use presence-aware authoring representations, reusing PartialRequestDefaults where appropriate.

Header empty-string deletion markers must survive until all existing header layers have been combined. Dropping a marker early must not restore an inherited header. Preserve header validation, ownership, and size limits.

Validate the final merged variant against model capabilities and adaptor restrictions. Preserved settings that conflict with a newly selected endpoint must produce an actionable validation error, not be silently discarded.

Preserve positions of existing variants; append newly created IDs in a deterministic order. Resolve default_variant after applying configuration and reject named defaults that are missing or disabled.

docs.title: 1. Disabling variants
docs.text:
Recommendation: introduce optional enabled, with omission equivalent to true.

[providers.openai.models."model-id".variants.low]
enabled = false

Proposed boundaries:

  • enabled = false removes an existing variant.
  • Disabling an absent variant is a valid no-op, including for custom providers.
  • Reject other variant settings alongside enabled = false rather than ignore them.
  • A default pointing to a disabled variant is invalid.

The user has not yet confirmed this replacement for operation = "disable".

docs.title: 2. Clearing reasoning
docs.text: Recommendation: omission preserves existing reasoning, with no new explicit clear mechanism in this change. TOML has no null. A thinking-off toggle or a none effort value is a concrete behavior, not removal of the setting.

docs.title: 3. Endpoint defaults and adaptor support
docs.text:
Recommendation: omitted request_endpoint preserves each adaptor's current native endpoint; custom openai-compatible continues to use Chat Completions. An explicit selection must be supported by that adaptor or rejected.

Before coding, enumerate the supported combinations, including how existing endpoint-specific adaptor IDs interact with an explicit endpoint choice and whether generic compatible Responses requires oven-sdk changes. Preserve provider-specific routing such as Azure deployment paths; the conventional paths above are not universal URL-construction instructions.

docs.title: 4. Pricing fallback and validation
docs.text: Recommendation: relocate authoring without changing existing rate precedence, missing-rate behavior, accounting precision, or historical session accounting. Verify these against crates/engine/src/usage.rs and session reconstruction before defining the final migration tests. Decide how to validate model-local pricing for disabled or unavailable catalog models. Do not silently introduce field-by-field catalog price inheritance while moving the schema.

docs.title: Proposed Qwen Configuration
docs.text:
This example uses the proposed names and three requested effort variants. It leaves default_variant unspecified. All three variants inherit sampling and API selection from the model; only reasoning effort differs.

[providers.cookie-api.models."qwen3.8-flash"]
# Existing display name and capabilities remain unchanged.
generation_options = { temperature = 1.0, top_p = 0.95 }
adaptor_options = { request_endpoint = "completions" }

[providers.cookie-api.models."qwen3.8-flash".variants.low]
reasoning = { type = "effort", value = "low" }

[providers.cookie-api.models."qwen3.8-flash".variants.medium]
reasoning = { type = "effort", value = "medium" }

[providers.cookie-api.models."qwen3.8-flash".variants.xhigh]
reasoning = { type = "effort", value = "xhigh" }

This is a partial model configuration, not a standalone valid provider. No credentials belong in this document. Configuring effort requests it from the backend; successful parsing or HTTP acceptance does not prove that the deployed Qwen server implements distinct effort behavior.

docs.title: Compatibility and Migration
docs.text:
After implementation, reject removed authored keys instead of accepting aliases:

  • operation in variants
  • defaults and options in model/variant configuration
  • top-level model shape
  • api_path in adaptor configuration
  • cancellation in authored model capabilities
  • top-level pricing
  • model_overrides, replaced by models for managed providers

Update relevant schemas, compiler errors, examples, and tests together. Keep authored-config changes distinct from runtime manifests, protocol contracts, and best-effort session history. Inventory persisted representations and either retain their intentional contracts or explicitly plan necessary version changes; do not mechanically rename shared serialized fields without checking consumers.

Migrate the user's local config only after the new binary is available. Preserve provider endpoints, credentials, capabilities, unrelated settings, and the current default-variant selection. Verify exact current contents before editing. Do not commit the local config or expose credentials in logs.

docs.title: Implementation Plan After Approval
docs.text:
1. Resolve open decisions and inventory all authoring and persisted consumers.
  2. Implement strict field renames, unified models authoring, catalog-model sparse overrides, presence-aware capability defaults, and presence-aware variant configuration.
  3. Implement base-model inheritance, sparse variant merging, and final validation.
  4. Implement endpoint selection through the complete adaptor execution path; remove the unused path setting and resolve automatic native replay for the effective endpoint while preserving explicit declarations. Derive runtime cancellation capability instead of accepting it from authored configuration. Implement wire model-ID overrides and block-specific replay eligibility, including encrypted reasoning's same-wire-model requirement.
  5. Relocate pricing with unchanged accounting semantics unless separately approved.
  6. Update tests, generated schemas/bindings where affected, and user docs.
  7. Review, fix findings, run gates, commit/push when authorized, and verify CI for the exact final SHA.
  8. Install the binary, migrate and validate local Qwen configuration, then run the established dev-artifact cleanup while preserving release/caches/sessions.

docs.title: Acceptance Tests
docs.text:
• New variant creation and sparse updates to generated catalog variants.
  • Managed models entries preserve omitted catalog fields and unmentioned catalog models; omitted or empty variant maps retain generated variants.
  • Model-level generation/adaptor overrides merge sparsely, including explicit false and empty lists. Custom model definitions still require their fields.
  • Unknown managed model IDs and forbidden capability overrides remain errors; explicit model disabling works without replacing the catalog collection.
  • Custom reasoning-only variants inherit base generation/adaptor settings.
  • Managed variants resolve base, catalog variant, and user variant fields in that order; unspecified catalog fields must not mask the base.
  • A single-field variant override preserves other inherited fields; base edits propagate only to fields not overridden by a later layer.
  • Omitted fields preserve values; explicit false and empty lists take effect.
  • Reasoning object replacement cannot create an invalid mixed behavior.
  • Header normalization and inherited-header deletion remain correct.
  • Deterministic ordering and default-variant resolution.
  • Approved disabling semantics, including absent IDs and conflicting fields.
  • Removed and unknown authored keys fail with clear errors.
  • Omitted tool calling, parallel tool calls, and structured output resolve to true only in the absence of inherited declarations. Explicit false values survive parsing and managed inheritance.
  • Missing catalog capability information uses the new true defaults rather than legacy projection fallbacks. Conflicting tool/parallel declarations and unsupported adaptor capabilities produce actionable errors.
  • Authored cancellation is rejected; current custom and managed models receive derived local-only cancellation. Existing interruption behavior remains intact.
  • Custom and managed generation/adaptor configuration validates consistently.
  • Endpoint choices select the correct encoder, route, stream decoder, and tool-call handling; invalid adaptor combinations fail before network access.
  • Omitted native replay enables valid artifact capture and reuse on supported adaptors/endpoints and resolves to unsupported elsewhere; explicit values and inherited catalog declarations remain distinguishable from absence.
  • Variant endpoint changes recompute automatic replay support; explicit incompatible capability declarations fail validation.
  • Standard supported blocks survive variant, model, provider, endpoint, header, and deployment-fingerprint changes without duplication. Wire tests confirm replay, including cross-provider and Azure revision-change/missing-revision cases, not merely successful configuration compilation.
  • Encrypted reasoning replays for equal effective wire model IDs and is excluded for different or unknown source IDs. Test aliases with the same wire ID and the same alias with a variant-level wire-ID override. Mixed-content artifacts preserve eligible standard blocks when safe to separate.
  • Model-ID resolution follows provider -> configured model -> configured variant; request dispatch and frozen reconstruction use the resolved ID while local selection and pricing identity remain unchanged.
  • Adaptor identity differences do not reject artifacts with supported encoding formats. Incompatible formats and invalid artifacts are not replayed, and protocol-required native state is not silently discarded. Explicit replay disabling remains effective and provider rejection is surfaced. Cache configuration remains independent.
  • Pricing relocation preserves decimal precision, rate precedence, missing-rate handling, and historical accounting as defined after the inventory.
  • Config layer replacement semantics do not accidentally become deep merges.
  • Existing title and compaction internal-agent flows remain functional.
  • Qwen low/medium/xhigh parse and compile; tests verify emitted effort values without claiming unsupported backend behavior.

docs.title: Verification Gates
docs.text:
Follow the repository's current AGENTS.md, including:

cargo build --locked --workspace --all-targets
cargo test --locked --workspace
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo +stable clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo +1.88.0 clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
crates/protocol/scripts/check-schema-additive.sh
RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' ./scripts/build-docs.sh
cargo deny --locked check advisories licenses sources

If oven-sdk changes are required, apply its own review and verification workflow before updating cookie-agent's pinned dependency revision.

docs.title: Source Pointers
docs.text:
• crates/models/src/model_types.rs: current defaults, options, reasoning, and variant directive types.
  • crates/models/src/authoring/mod.rs: custom/managed authoring and partial defaults.
  • crates/models/src/compiler/variants.rs: generated variants, directives, and default resolution.
  • crates/models/src/compiler/dynamic.rs: validation and header composition.
  • crates/models/src/compiler/executable.rs: executable adaptor configuration.
  • crates/models/src/manager/mod.rs: variant runtime compilation.
  • crates/config/src/runtime.rs: current pricing authoring types.
  • crates/config/src/loader.rs: configuration layer behavior.
  • crates/engine/src/usage.rs and crates/engine/src/session.rs: pricing and session accounting.

No code changes are authorized by the existence of this draft.

docs.title: Plugins: Tools, Hooks, Events, and Producers
docs.text: Status: implemented (decisions of 2026-10-16). Section Implementation notes records where the code settled details differently. This document is the governing specification for cleaning up the plugin protocol, host, SDK, and configuration: plugin tools speak the runtime protocol's tool messages, the host runs on the runtime stack, and dead or half-built parts go. This spec was written while there were no plugin implementations outside this repository, so every part of the plugin protocol could change. The compatibility spec now governs how the plugin protocol changes: it is versioned by semver, and plugins written for one major keep working with every daemon of that major. Section Decisions records what review settled.

docs.title: 1. Goal and scope
docs.text:
A plugin does four things: it declares tools, intercepts engine hooks, streams session events and a bus, and produces messages. Runtimes (runtimes spec) do tools far better than plugins do today: a prepare step with the tool's own approval identity, progress, background, cancellation, media, collision and concurrency choices, tools_changed, and prompt sections, where a plugin tool is one plugin/tools/call under a shared plugin:<label> permission. The plugin host also carries its own process supervisor, JSON-RPC loop, framing, and SDK, none of which shares the runtime stack's stderr capture, restart, or status reporting.

After this work a plugin is a trusted, local, daemon-wide extension that declares tools the way a runtime does, intercepts hooks, watches events, publishes to the bus, and produces messages to any session, over the runtime stack's transport and process handling.

Out of scope: remote plugins, hooks in runtimes, event replay and filters, plugin resources, and a runtime SDK.

docs.title: 2. Plugin tools speak the runtime tool messages
docs.text:
A plugin declares and runs tools with the runtime protocol's tool messages, unchanged, over its own connection (runtime protocol):

Message Direction As in the runtime protocol tools in the plugin/initialize result plugin → daemon tools and prompt_sections of RuntimeTools, each tool a ToolDeclaration runtime/tools_changed plugin → daemon the plugin's tool list changed tool/prepare, tool/revalidate, tool/release daemon → plugin the plugin prepares calls and reports their approval identity, normalized arguments, and presentation tool/execute, tool/progress both execution with streamed output and media tool/cancel daemon → plugin cancellation reaches the plugin tool/detachable plugin → daemon background calls and reports_itself
  • Declarations are the runtime's: an optional, free-form permission action (a plugin tool may need none, or name its own action such as browse), collision, concurrency, result_truncation, output, background, and background_default. primary_resource_param goes: the plugin computes its permission resource in tool/prepare.
  • The daemon reuses its runtime tool client for a plugin's tools, so approval, progress, background, cancellation, media retention, and tools_changed behave exactly as for a runtime's.
  • Publication. Plugin tools stay in the global runtime, but each plugin is its own source when names are composed, so its prefix is the plugin's name rather than global. When a plugin tool's name is taken by another tool (another plugin's, an MCP server's, global's own, or any attached runtime's), its declared collision decides:
  • prefix (the default): it is published as <plugin>_<tool>, the other tool keeps its name, as runtime tools are prefixed with their attachment name today;
  • override, a new collision value: it takes the bare name, and the tool it overrides is published under its own source's prefix (or hidden, if that tool is fallback). Two override tools with one name are both prefixed, with a diagnostic. Base-layer names stay reserved: no plugin or runtime tool takes them. override is part of the shared ToolCollision, so a runtime tool may declare it too. The MCP crate no longer knows about plugins.
  • Removed: plugin/tools/call, ExtensionToolDeclaration, ExtensionToolCallParams, ExtensionToolCallResult, the tools capability (declaring tools is the capability), [plugins.<name>] tool_timeout_ms (a runtime call has no per-call timeout; a tool bounds its own work), the plugin permission action and every plugin: special case (permission-name mapping and rule matching, the CLI's --allowed-tools plugin and plugin:<name>, the TUI's "plugin tools" row), and the MCP crate's plugin claims (claim_plugin_tools, plugin_owns_tool, release_plugin_tools, the collision handler, and MCP preempting a plugin). A stored rule naming plugin stays a valid free-form label.
  • Shared types. The runtime protocol's tool wire types (ToolDeclaration, the prepare, execute, progress, and detach params and results, and the JSON-RPC peer and line transport) move from runtime_api into the Apache-2.0 protocol crate, so the Apache-2.0 plugin SDK can use them; runtime_api re-exports them.
  • SDK. The plugin SDK's tool builder takes the runtime declaration and gives an execute closure progress, detach, cancellation, and producers; the echo example is updated.

Hooks, events, and producers stay daemon-wide: a session that detaches global loses plugin tools, as it loses every global tool, and keeps its hooks, events, and producers.

docs.title: 3. Protocol cleanup
docs.text:
The plugin protocol keeps its own methods but takes the runtime protocol's shape where they meet.

Version. An integer, starting at 1 (today's string "0.0.8" goes), checked as the runtime protocol checks its version.

Removed as dead:

Item Why resources and publish_session_events capabilities Never implemented; publishing is always rejected. ExtensionEmitResultParams.durable Always rejected; emit_result reports the bus outcome only. The engine capability flags other than producer_messaging Always true. ExtensionToolAfterResultResult.note Never read. ExtensionAgentBeforeStartResult.addendum Duplicates append_to_system_prompt. ExtensionMessageEndParams.role Always assistant. plugin/ping Used only by tests; liveness is the connection itself. provider_before_headers hook The model adapters do not expose request headers, so it can neither see nor change them. headers of provider_after_response Always empty; the hook keeps status.

Renamed: ExtensionModelSelectSource::FallbackRestore becomes fallback, which is when the engine sends it.

Shared with runtimes. The producer params and results (ExtensionProducer*, ExtensionRecovery*) move to neutral names (ProducerRegisterParams, …, RecoveryCompleteParams) in the protocol crate, used by both protocols. The plugin methods become producer/register, producer/send, producer/unregister, producer/discard, producer/recovery/start, and producer/recovery/complete, the runtime protocol's names.

Hook payloads. tool_before_call and tool_after_result gain the call's origin: { "kind": "runtime", "attachment": "<name>", "runtime_id": "<id>" } for a runtime's or plugin's tool, { "kind": "base" } for a daemon base tool, so a hook can tell local's bash from a remote runtime's.

docs.title: 4. Host fixes
docs.text:
• Per-hook contexts. Each hook invocation gets its own context ID. Today one ID is shared by the four hooks of a model attempt, so a plugin's plugin/emit from the second hook on is rejected as spent.
  • Typed hook failures. A hook failure is classified once, by kind (timeout, crashed, disconnected, rejected, malformed), instead of by matching error strings in five places, so a malformed reply is no longer recorded as a timeout.
  • Engine diagnostics are not plugin diagnostics. Automatic compaction's "disabled after 3 failures" notice gets its own runless event instead of a plugin_diagnostic under the made-up plugin name engine:auto-compact.
  • Dead code. PluginConfig::validate and ConfigError::Plugin, the plugin-origin self-exclusion of streamed events, the EventParamsRef and BusEventParamsRef duplicates of the protocol structs, and plugin_statuses outside the new status RPC.
  • Old logs. plugin_event_added and the recovery_failed and recovery_disabled kinds of plugin_diagnostic are never written; they stay decodable and rendered for old session logs.

docs.title: 5. Host on the runtime stack
docs.text:
The plugin host drops its own process and transport code and uses the runtime stack's:

  • Process. Started like a runtime process: an argv, env, cwd, its own process group (a job object on Windows), and stderr captured into a bounded diagnostic tail instead of inherited, which today can corrupt the TUI's screen.
  • Transport. The runtime protocol's JSON-RPC peer and line transport, with its 48 MiB frame bound, replacing the hand-rolled reader, writer, pending-request table, and 4 MiB bound.
  • Restart. A plugin that exits or drops its connection is restarted with the runtime reconnect policy (1 s, 2 s, 4 s, then failed until the user retries). A restarted plugin gets a new connection epoch; its producers register again and recover as on first start.
  • Status. Client RPCs plugins.list (name, state, capabilities and hooks, last failure with the stderr tail) and plugins.restart, a plugins.changed notification, and a TUI plugins view (/plugins) next to the runtimes view.

docs.title: 6. Configuration
docs.text:
[plugins.audit]
command = ["python3", "audit.py"]
env = { AUDIT_LOG = "~/audit.log" }
cwd = "~/plugins"
enabled = true
producer_messaging = false
interception_timeout_ms = 2000
startup_timeout_ms = 10000
shutdown_grace_ms = 3000
  • command becomes an argv array, as in [runtimes.<id>]; args goes.
  • tool_timeout_ms goes with plugin tools.
  • Plugins still run hooks in the order the file lists them.

docs.title: 7. Phases
docs.text:
Each phase lands as its own commits with every gate green, and is pushed.

  1. Clean the protocol. Section 3 and 4: dead fields, capabilities, and hooks removed, shared producer types and producer/* method names, integer version 1, origins in tool hooks, and the host fixes; the SDK and fixtures follow.
  2. Runtime stack and status. Section 5 and 6: process, transport, restart, stderr capture, plugins.list / plugins.restart / plugins.changed, the TUI view, the command array.
  3. Plugin tools. Section 2: the wire types moved to the protocol crate, plugin tools over the runtime tool messages and the daemon's runtime tool client, each plugin its own composition source with prefix and the new override collision, the plugin action and the MCP crate's plugin claims removed, the SDK's tool builder.
  4. Documentation. The plugin guide and development pages rewritten (dropping the crate-internal sections and stale versions), goal-mode and runtime references; this spec marked implemented.

docs.title: 8. Decisions
docs.text:
Decided 2026-10-16:

  • Plugins keep tools, hooks, events, the bus, and producers.
  • Plugin tools speak the runtime protocol's tool messages, and the daemon runs them with its runtime tool client.
  • Plugins may produce to any session.

Confirmed in review 2026-10-16:

  • Remove provider_before_headers rather than wire headers through the model adapters.
  • Remove plugin/ping.
  • Restart crashed plugins with the runtime reconnect policy.
  • Rename the producer methods to producer/* and share their types.
  • Move the runtime protocol's tool wire types and JSON-RPC peer into the Apache-2.0 protocol crate for the plugin SDK.
  • Drop tool_timeout_ms; a plugin bounds its own tool work, as a runtime does.
  • A colliding plugin tool is prefixed with its plugin's name, or, when it declares collision: override, takes the bare name and pushes the other tool to its prefix.

docs.title: 9. Implementation notes
docs.text:
Landed 2026-10-16, with phases 1 to 3 in one change because the host's tests would otherwise have been rewritten twice.

  • The status RPCs are plugins.list and plugins.restart, matching runtimes.list and runtimes.reconnect. They, the engine_diagnostic event, and the removed plugin action are client protocol 44.
  • Hook failures are timeout, disconnected (not connected, or the connection ended during the hook, recorded as interception_crash), rejected (an error answer), and malformed; the last two record the new interception_rejected diagnostic. unsupported_capability is kept only for old logs.
  • EventParamsRef and BusEventParamsRef stay: they borrow the event so it is serialized once for every subscribed plugin, and a test pins them to the protocol structs' wire form.
  • A plugin's first failed start is reconnecting like a later drop, and is failed once the reconnect policy is exhausted.
  • Plugin request IDs are integers, as the shared peer requires.
  • Every plugin's tool provider shares the reserved provenance ID plugin.

docs.title: Refactor Phase 1: Test Layout and Build Hygiene
docs.text:
Status: implemented. Part of the architecture refresh recorded in Refactor phase 1, phase 2, and phase 3.

Repository: this workspace (paths below are relative to the workspace root). Branch: refactor/phase-1-tests-and-build-hygiene (from main)

Hard constraints - Pure reorganisation. No production behavior change. No test body edits beyond use paths, module paths, and visibility. - Test counts must not change: cargo test -p cookie_agent_engine --lib -- --list | grep -c ': test$' is 637 before and after; cargo test -p cookie_agent_tui --lib -- --list | grep -c ': test$' is 535 before and after. Check every crate you touch the same way. - Follow AGENTS.md: conventional commit subjects (refactor(engine): ...), locked builds, fmt + clippy -D warnings on stable and +1.88.0. - Keep insta snapshots byte-identical. Snapshot files move with their tests; only their file names may change when a module path changes.

docs.title: A1. Move runtime_tests.rs and its six child files into crates/engine/src/runtime/tests/
docs.text:
Today crates/engine/src/lib.rs declares #[cfg(test)] mod runtime_tests; and runtime_tests.rs (24.5k lines, 178 tests) declares six #[path] children: producer_runtime_tests (which itself has child goal_reminder_runtime_tests), producer_plugin_tests, producer_discard_tests, delegation_revert_tests, goal_selection_tests, messaging_tests.

Target layout:

crates/engine/src/runtime/tests/
  mod.rs            // #[cfg(test)] root: `mod support; mod admission; ...` plus nothing else
  support.rs        // shared fixtures moved verbatim from runtime_tests.rs:
                    //   pub(crate) struct Fixture, private_tempdir, create_private_test_dir,
                    //   write_private_test_file, copy_private_test_tree, python_command,
                    //   test_timeout, TestFlag, PanicResistantTempDir, test_turn_context,
                    //   every Test*Provider / Test*Executor / OrderedToolDefinitionProvider, etc.
  <topic>.rs        // one file per topic, each `use super::support::*;` (and whatever else it needs)
  producers.rs               // was producer_runtime_tests.rs
  goal_reminders.rs          // was goal_reminder_runtime_tests.rs (child of producers.rs today; make it a sibling)
  producers_plugin.rs        // was producer_plugin_tests.rs
  producers_discard.rs       // was producer_discard_tests.rs
  delegation_revert.rs       // was delegation_revert_tests.rs
  goal_selection.rs          // was goal_selection_tests.rs
  messaging.rs               // was messaging_tests.rs

Declaration: in crates/engine/src/runtime.rs add #[cfg(test)] mod tests; (Rust resolves runtime/tests/mod.rs automatically). Remove mod runtime_tests; from lib.rs. Delete the seven old files.

Topic split of the 178 tests currently in runtime_tests.rs: group by what the test name and body exercise. Suggested files (create only the ones that get tests; add others if a clear cluster emerges): admission.rs, approvals.rs, artifacts.rs, compaction.rs, delegation.rs, mailbox.rs (steer / cancel / stdin / subscribe), model_loop.rs (retry, fallback, attempts), permissions.rs, plugins.rs, recovery.rs, sessions.rs (create / resume / revert / fork / rename), skills.rs, tool_execution.rs, usage.rs, misc.rs for the remainder. No file over ~3000 lines. Test function names are unchanged.

Anything in runtime_tests.rs that is referenced from non-test code paths via pub(crate) (e.g. Fixture) keeps pub(crate) in support.rs; grep for runtime_tests:: across the crate and fix every path.

docs.title: A2. Collapse the 26 #[cfg(test)] hook fields on Inner into one struct
docs.text:
New file crates/engine/src/runtime/test_hooks.rs, whole file #![cfg(test)] (declare with #[cfg(test)] pub(crate) mod test_hooks; in runtime.rs).

Move these type definitions there from runtime.rs (lines ~594-712 today, all already #[cfg(test)]): PromptSnapshotHook, PagingRaceHook, ToolProgressAppendBlock, ReadOnlyReopenHook, ApprovalEvaluationHook, ModelRetrySleepMode, ModelRetrySleepHook (+ its impl), AdmissionConfirmationHook, ResumeAdmissionHook, AdmissionBlockingHook, AbandonedSweepHook. Give them pub(crate) visibility.

#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct TestHooks {
    pub(crate) prompt_snapshot_hook: Mutex<Option<Arc<PromptSnapshotHook>>>,
    pub(crate) prompt_before_claim_hook: Mutex<Option<Arc<PromptSnapshotHook>>>,
    pub(crate) janitor_before_barrier_hook: Mutex<Option<Arc<PagingRaceHook>>>,
    pub(crate) compaction_execution_hook: Mutex<Option<Arc<PagingRaceHook>>>,
    pub(crate) read_only_reopen_hook: Mutex<Option<ReadOnlyReopenHook>>,
    pub(crate) approval_evaluation_hook: Mutex<Option<Arc<ApprovalEvaluationHook>>>,
    pub(crate) model_retry_sleep_hook: ModelRetrySleepHook,
    pub(crate) pending_approval_ready: tokio::sync::Notify,
    pub(crate) admission_confirmation_hook: Mutex<Option<Arc<AdmissionConfirmationHook>>>,
    pub(crate) resume_admission_hook: Mutex<Option<Arc<ResumeAdmissionHook>>>,
    pub(crate) resume_attachment_hook: Mutex<Option<Arc<ResumeAdmissionHook>>>,
    pub(crate) skill_fork_reservation_hook: Mutex<Option<Arc<PagingRaceHook>>>,
    pub(crate) producer_wake_hook: Mutex<Option<Arc<PagingRaceHook>>>,
    pub(crate) delegation_reservation_hook: Mutex<Option<Arc<PagingRaceHook>>>,
    pub(crate) resume_rollback_hook: Mutex<Option<Arc<ResumeAdmissionHook>>>,
    pub(crate) admission_blocking_hook: Mutex<Option<AdmissionBlockingHook>>,
    pub(crate) abandoned_sweep_hook: Mutex<Option<AbandonedSweepHook>>,
    pub(crate) plugin_diagnostic_append_block: Mutex<Option<Arc<tokio::sync::Notify>>>,
    pub(crate) tool_progress_append_block: Mutex<Option<Arc<ToolProgressAppendBlock>>>,
    pub(crate) publication_failure: AtomicBool,
    pub(crate) delegate_start_failures: AtomicU64,
    pub(crate) delegate_start_failure_observed: tokio::sync::Notify,
    pub(crate) delegate_terminal_append_failures: AtomicU64,
    pub(crate) run_setup_append_failures: AtomicU64,
    pub(crate) resume_monitor_failures: AtomicU64,
    pub(crate) adoption_reconcile_failures: AtomicU64,
}

Field names are kept exactly so the change is a prefix rewrite. Inner gets a single #[cfg(test)] pub(crate) test_hooks: TestHooks, and every self.inner.<hook> / inner.<hook> becomes self.inner.test_hooks.<hook>. If ModelRetrySleepHook::default() is not derivable, implement Default for TestHooks by hand. Engine::open initialises the field with TestHooks::default().

docs.title: A3. Move every inline test module of 500+ lines into its own file (workspace-wide)
docs.text:
Rule: if a #[cfg(test)] mod tests { ... } (or similarly named) block at the end of src/<name>.rs is 500 lines or more, cut its body into src/<name>/tests.rs and replace the block with #[cfg(test)] mod tests;. The module path is unchanged, so use super::*; keeps working. If <name>.rs already has a <name>/ directory (e.g. session/projection.rs, runtime/compaction/tests.rs), place the file there; where a tests.rs already exists, name the new one after its module (e.g. windows_tests.rs) and keep the declaration.

Known candidates (line counts of the test tail today): engine session.rs 3449 (two modules: tests and windows_tests), events.rs 3247, model_history.rs 2571, permissions.rs 1632, plugin.rs 1091, goal_projection.rs 821, runtime/output_capture.rs 654, runtime/artifacts.rs 593, runtime/compaction.rs 550; tui state/mod.rs 2982 (becomes state/tests.rs), markdown.rs 1194, ui/input.rs 831, ui/goal.rs 814, lib.rs 793 (becomes src/tests.rs), theme.rs 745, ui/management.rs 571, ui/pickers.rs 507; protocol session/client.rs 1196 (already has session/client/tests.rs, so name it accordingly or merge if it is the same module); plugin_sdk server.rs 1109; cookie_agent main.rs 1124 (it is a binary; src/tests.rs declared from main.rs); models manager/mod.rs 911; tools read.rs 861, lib.rs 498 (skip, under threshold), edit.rs 493 (skip). Re-derive the list with a script rather than trusting these numbers.

Insta: snapshot files live in snapshots/ next to the source file that contains the test. Moving a test module into a subdirectory moves its expected snapshot directory. git mv the affected .snap files, then run cargo insta test --workspace --unreferenced=reject (or cargo insta test followed by cargo insta pending-snapshots) and confirm zero new or changed snapshots. Snapshot contents must not change.

docs.title: A4. TUI transcript.rs test split
docs.text:
crates/tui/src/ui/transcript.rs has 140 tests in mod tests from line ~4789 to the end (20.4k lines). Target:

crates/tui/src/ui/transcript/tests/
  mod.rs        // `mod support; mod layout; ...`
  support.rs    // shared helpers / fixtures currently at the top of `mod tests`
  <topic>.rs    // e.g. layout.rs, scrolling.rs, assistant.rs, tool_rows.rs, diffs.rs, read_output.rs,
                //      approvals.rs, pickers.rs, selection.rs, goal.rs, producers.rs, misc.rs

Declare with #[cfg(test)] mod tests; in transcript.rs. Keep the small #[cfg(test)] helper functions that live in the production part of transcript.rs (e.g. transcript_layout_with*) where they are. The 10 insta snapshots named cookie_agent_tui__ui__transcript__tests__<name>.snap become cookie_agent_tui__ui__transcript__tests__<topic>__<name>.snap; rename them with git mv into crates/tui/src/ui/transcript/tests/snapshots/, then verify with cargo insta test that nothing is new or changed. No test file over ~3000 lines.

ui/app.rs keeps #[path = "fallback_tests.rs"] mod fallback_tests; as is (already external). Its tiny post_teardown_tests module may stay inline.

docs.title: Part B: build hygiene (item 7)
docs.text:
B1. Workspace Cargo.toml: add

[profile.dev]
debug = "line-tables-only"

(keep [profile.dist] as is; test inherits dev). Do not add split-debuginfo.

B2. Delete the two untracked stray build directories: vendor/syntect/target (788 MB) and vendor/bincode-compat/ (only contains target/, 99 MB, not tracked by git). Confirm with git status --short vendor that nothing tracked is affected.

B3. After B1 and after all of Part A is committed and verified, run cargo clean once in the workspace root (the target dir is 649 GB; the profile change makes the old artifacts stale anyway). Then run the full local gate one final time from a cold cache so the final push is verified against what CI will build. Report the new du -sh target after the cold gate.

docs.title: Commits (suggested order)
docs.text:
1. refactor(engine): move runtime tests under runtime/tests and split by topic
  2. refactor(engine): collect Inner test hooks into TestHooks
  3. refactor: move large inline test modules into sibling files (may be several commits per crate)
  4. refactor(tui): split transcript tests by topic
  5. build: emit line-tables-only debuginfo in dev profile

docs.title: Local gate (run before every push)
docs.text:
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo build --locked --workspace --all-targets
cargo +stable clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo +1.88.0 clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --locked --workspace
cargo doc --locked --workspace --no-deps   # with RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings
cargo deny --locked check advisories licenses sources
cargo insta test --workspace   # zero new/changed snapshots
(crates/protocol/scripts/check-bindings.sh --check is unaffected by this phase; run it only if you touch crates/protocol.)

docs.title: Milestone
docs.text: Push the branch, wait for the GitHub Actions CI workflow on the branch to be green (gh run list --branch <branch>; gh run watch <id> --exit-status --interval 60, repeatedly if it exceeds a tool timeout; a run takes ~50 min). Fix and re-push on failure. When green: git checkout main && git merge --ff-only <branch> && git push origin main, then wait for the CI run on main to be green as well. Report: main SHA, CI run URLs, before/after test counts per crate, the largest remaining file sizes, and du -sh target.

docs.title: Refactor Phase 2: Dependencies, Bindings, CI, and Syntect
docs.text:
Status: implemented on 2026-09-21. Part of the architecture refresh recorded in Refactor phase 1, phase 2, and phase 3.

Repository: this workspace (paths below are relative to the workspace root). Sibling repo (author-owned): ../oven_sdk (sibling checkout of cookie-agent/oven-sdk) (GitHub cookie-agent/oven-sdk), currently at rev 1b99edc930651a82930ab4de475a82a33ba6cdd5 which is exactly what cookie-agent pins. Branch: refactor/phase-2-deps-bindings-ci-syntect (from main, after phase 1 has merged)

Hard constraints - No runtime behavior change. Tests that only existed to guard the removed machinery (vendored syntect hashes, TypeScript bindings) are deleted; everything else keeps passing unchanged. - AGENTS.md rules apply (strict config, no compat shims, conventional commits, locked builds, fmt/clippy on stable + 1.88). - crates/models/tests/release_integrity.rs is a policy test suite that asserts on Cargo.toml, deny.toml, CI YAML and the vendor tree. Update its assertions to the new policy in the same commit as each change; do not weaken checks that still apply (pinned oven rev, exact internal versions, pinned CI actions, no secret material).

docs.title: 3a. Single reqwest (0.13) by updating oven-sdk
docs.text:
In oven_sdk (branch from its main): - Workspace Cargo.toml: reqwest = { version = "0.13", default-features = false, features = ["json", "stream", "rustls"] } (0.13 renamed the TLS feature; adapt to whatever 0.13.4's feature names actually are). - Fix API breaks in every crate that uses reqwest (oven-sdk transport, provider crates). Run cargo build --workspace --all-targets, cargo test --workspace, clippy -D warnings, cargo deny check if the repo has a deny.toml. - reqwest types are part of oven-sdk's public API (cookie-agent constructs reqwest::Client and hands it to oven adapters), so bump each oven crate's minor version (0.5.0 -> 0.6.0, 0.6.0 -> 0.7.0, 0.4.0 -> 0.5.0, 0.3.0 -> 0.4.0) in the same commit. - Commit chore(deps)!: move to reqwest 0.13, push to origin main of oven-sdk, record the new commit SHA.

In cookie-agent: - Workspace Cargo.toml: every oven-sdk* entry gets the new version = "=x.y.z" and the new rev. Delete the reqwest-oven alias. Add one workspace entry reqwest = { version = "=0.13.4", default-features = false, features = ["json", "stream", "rustls"] } and switch crates/engine/Cargo.toml and crates/tools/Cargo.toml to reqwest.workspace = true; crates/models/Cargo.toml uses reqwest.workspace = true and its sources use reqwest:: instead of reqwest_oven:: (catalog/transport.rs, adapters/oven.rs). - cargo update -p reqwest@0.12.28 --precise-style removal is not needed; just regenerate Cargo.lock with cargo update -w limited to the changed packages (cargo update -p oven-sdk -p oven-sdk-openai ...), then confirm cargo tree --workspace -d -e normal shows exactly one reqwest, one hyper, one hyper-util, one rustls, one h2, one tower, one tower-http. - deny.toml: the comment names the old rev; update it. release_integrity::oven_dependencies_use_one_pinned_git_revision_with_exact_publish_versions and any other test that embeds the rev or the versions: update.

docs.title: 3b. Engine no longer depends on oven-sdk-azure / oven-sdk-openai
docs.text:
The only use is crates/engine/src/runtime/compaction.rs:18-19, ~404-416, where a native compaction request gets provider-specific instructions via the two extension traits, keyed on the adapter id strings "oven.openai.responses" and "oven.azure.openai.responses".

Add to crates/models/src/adapters/ a new module compaction.rs:

//! Provider-specific native compaction request options.

use oven_sdk::CompactionRequest; // use whatever the concrete request type in compaction.rs is

/// Attach provider-native compaction instructions for adapters that support them.
/// Adapters without a native option leave the request untouched.
pub fn with_native_compaction_instructions(
    request: CompactionRequest,
    adapter_id: &str,          // the same string the engine matches on today
    instructions: String,
) -> CompactionRequest

(If there is already an OvenAdapterFamily enum that these ids map to, take it instead of &str; the engine then passes the family it already has.) Re-export from cookie_agent_models::adapters. The engine's match block becomes one call. Remove oven-sdk-azure and oven-sdk-openai from crates/engine/Cargo.toml. Move any engine unit test that covered the two branches to the models crate, unchanged in substance.

docs.title: 3c. Remaining duplicate versions
docs.text: After 3a, run cargo tree --workspace -d -e normal --depth 1. For each duplicate, attempt the cheapest unification and keep it only if it needs no code change beyond imports: - fancy-regex 0.16 (syntect) vs 0.19 (jsonschema): after Item 6 moves syntect to crates.io, check whether a newer syntect 5.x on crates.io already uses fancy-regex 0.19 (cargo search syntect --limit 1 / cargo info syntect); if so, use it (exact-pin as the workspace does). - base64 0.23 (rmcp only), sha2/digest/block-buffer/cpufeatures/crypto-common 0.11-line (lopdf only), getrandom x3, rand x2, hashbrown x2, thiserror x2, windows-sys x2, nix, nom, syn, bitflags, weezl, wasm-streams, bit-set/bit-vec: these come from third-party crates; do not fork or patch to unify them. Report the final duplicate list in the summary as a before/after table.

docs.title: Item 4: drop the TypeScript bindings, keep JSON Schema for the additive checks
docs.text:
Decision: schemars derives stay everywhere (the tools crate embeds protocol types such as ToolCallId in its own JSON-schema tool argument structs, so the derives are a runtime requirement). ts-rs goes entirely.

  • Remove ts-rs from [workspace.dependencies], crates/identity/Cargo.toml, crates/protocol/Cargo.toml. Remove every #[derive(... TS ...)] entry and every #[ts(...)] attribute (≈634 derive sites across identity and protocol; keep the JsonSchema and #[schemars(...)] parts). Remove use ts_rs::TS imports.
  • crates/protocol/src/bindings.rs: delete the TypeScript export path and BindingExportError::TypeScript; keep the JSON-schema export used by the additive checks. crates/protocol/examples/generate.rs: emits only JSON schemas.
  • Delete from git: crates/protocol/generated/ (both json-schema/ and typescript/ outputs), crates/protocol/typescript/ (package.json, package-lock.json). Keep event-payload-baseline.json and extension-protocol-baseline.json; those are what the additive checks compare against.
  • Replace crates/protocol/scripts/check-bindings.sh with crates/protocol/scripts/check-schema-additive.sh: cargo run --locked -p cookie_agent_protocol --example generate -- --output <tmpdir> then the existing test-event-payload-additive.sh / test-extension-protocol-additive.sh logic against the baselines. No npm, no node. Python 3 only if the existing comparison already uses it. The script no longer has a --check mode (nothing is checked in any more), so update callers.
  • Update docs: docs/site/reference/schemas.md (no TypeScript, no checked-in generated tree), docs/site/reference/protocol.md, docs/site/architecture.md ("JSON Schema and TypeScript bindings" wording), AGENTS.md required gates (check-bindings.sh --check -> new script), and any include-markdown that pulled from generated/. ./scripts/build-docs.sh must still pass in strict mode.
  • release_integrity tests that reference the bindings script or npm: update.

docs.title: Item 5: CI diet
docs.text:
Rewrite .github/workflows/ci.yml (leave docs.yml, nightly-prune.yml, release.yml untouched). Keep every action pinned by full SHA as the repo does today; look up SHAs with gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/git/ref/tags/<tag>.

name: CI
on: [push, pull_request]
permissions: { contents: read }
jobs:
  stable:            # ubuntu-latest, toolchain stable, components rustfmt+clippy
    - Swatinem/rust-cache (pinned SHA, v2.x)
    - cargo fmt --all -- --check
    - cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings      # replaces build + check + clippy
    - cargo test --locked --workspace                                      # RUSTFLAGS=-D warnings
    - cargo doc --locked --workspace --no-deps                             # RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings
    - crates/protocol/scripts/check-schema-additive.sh
    - cargo test --locked -p cookie_agent_models --test release_integrity
    - cargo build --release --locked -p cookie_agent                       # only the binary, only for the secret scan below
    - cargo test --locked -p cookie_agent_models --test release_integrity release_binary_contains_no_secret_material -- --ignored --exact
    - taiki-e/install-action (pinned SHA) with tool: cargo-deny@0.20.2,cargo-audit@0.22.2
    - cargo audit --file Cargo.lock --deny yanked
    - cargo deny --locked check advisories licenses sources
  msrv:              # ubuntu-latest, toolchain 1.88.0, rust-cache
    - cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets                       # RUSTFLAGS=-D warnings
  windows:           # windows-latest x86_64 only, toolchain 1.88.0, rust-cache, timeout 90
    - cargo test --locked --workspace -- --nocapture                       # RUST_BACKTRACE=1
  release-targets:   # same 7-target matrix as today, but
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    - cargo check --locked --target ${{ matrix.target }} -p cookie_agent
  release:           # unchanged: needs [stable, msrv, windows, release-targets], same if:, uses release.yml

Drop: the duplicate cargo build --all-targets and cargo check --all-targets steps, the release build of the whole workspace with all targets, the MSRV job's full test/doc/release repetition, the windows-11-arm test runner (it stays in release-targets), the cargo install of audit/deny.

Update release_integrity::ci_supply_chain_and_release_gates_are_pinned (and neighbours) to assert the new shape: every uses: pinned by 40-hex SHA, cargo-deny and cargo-audit versions still pinned, release job still gated on all four jobs.

docs.title: Item 6: un-vendor syntect
docs.text:
• Workspace Cargo.toml: remove exclude = ["vendor/syntect"] and the [patch.crates-io] syntect = { path = "vendor/syntect" } block. syntect stays exact-pinned from crates.io: syntect = { version = "=5.3.0", default-features = false, features = ["default-syntaxes", "default-themes", "regex-fancy"] } (or the newer 5.x chosen in 3c).
  • git rm -r vendor/. Remove the vendor/** -text -whitespace line from .gitattributes.
  • deny.toml: keep ignore = ["RUSTSEC-2025-0141"] (bincode 1.x unmaintained; syntect 5.x still needs it) but rewrite the comment so it no longer refers to vendoring.
  • crates/models/tests/release_integrity.rs: delete syntect_patch_is_exactly_pinned_and_declared and vendored_syntect_matches_declared_upstream_delta; rename/adjust workspace_metadata_limits_publishing_and_uses_vendored_syntect to assert syntect is exact-pinned from crates.io with default-features = false; drop vendor/syntect/Cargo.toml from every_internal_path_dependency_has_its_exact_package_version; drop the --manifest -path vendor/ expectation in ci_supply_chain_and_release_gates_are_pinned.
  • crates/tui/src/markdown.rs tests around lines 2468-2488 include_bytes! the dump assets from ../../../vendor/syntect/assets/. Rewrite those tests to load through syntect's public API (SyntaxSet::load_defaults_newlines(), SyntaxSet::load_defaults_nonewlines(), ThemeSet::load_defaults()) and keep whatever they assert about the TUI's own rendering; delete assertions that only existed to prove the vendored dump bytes matched upstream.
  • Confirm cargo deny --locked check sources passes (crates.io source, no path patch), cargo build --locked resolves syntect from the registry, and the TUI highlighting tests pass.

docs.title: Commits (suggested order)
docs.text:
1. oven-sdk repo: chore(deps)!: move to reqwest 0.13 (+ version bumps), pushed first.
  2. chore(deps)!: unify on reqwest 0.13 via oven-sdk <short-sha>
  3. refactor(models): own provider-native compaction options

When green: git checkout main && git merge --ff-only <branch> && git push origin main; wait for CI and Documentation on main to be green. docs.title: Refactor Phase 3: Module Splits
docs.text:
Status: implemented on 2026-09-21. Part of the architecture refresh recorded in Refactor phase 1, phase 2, and phase 3.

Repository: this workspace (paths below are relative to the workspace root). Branch: refactor/phase-3-split-monoliths (from main, after phase 2 has merged)

Hard constraints - No behavior change, no public API change for downstream crates (server, tools, cookie_agent keep compiling without edits except import paths if a pub item's module moves; prefer re-exports so they need none). - Tests: no body edits beyond paths and renamed field accesses. Test counts unchanged. - One commit per sub-part (3A..3E), each leaving the workspace green on the full local gate. - AGENTS.md rules (conventional commits, locked builds, fmt/clippy on stable + 1.88).

docs.title: 3A. Engine Inner: group state by subsystem
docs.text:
crates/engine/src/runtime.rs pub(crate) struct Inner has 82 fields (52 mutexes). Keep the shared infrastructure flat and move per-subsystem state into structs owned by the module that already implements that subsystem. Field names drop their subsystem prefix. All new structs are pub(crate), #[derive(Default)] where every member is defaultable, constructed in Engine::open.

Stays flat on Inner: config, config_store, artifacts, store, delegation_events, grant_journal, model_manager, published_runtime, runtime_mutation, runtime_notifications, engine_events, manifest_store, tools, provider_ids, mcp, plugins, mcp_mutation, permissions, skills (the registry), runtime, runtime_revision_index, mutation_locks, janitor_task, #[cfg(test)] test_hooks.

New groups:

// runtime/delegation.rs
pub(crate) struct DelegationState {
    pub(crate) inflight: Mutex<HashMap<InvocationId, HashMap<u64, InflightDelegation>>>,   // was inflight_delegations
    pub(crate) by_session: Mutex<HashMap<SessionId, DelegationRecord>>,                    // was delegations_by_session
    pub(crate) queue: Mutex<VecDeque<SessionId>>,                                          // was delegation_queue
    pub(crate) admission: tokio::sync::Mutex<()>,                                          // was delegation_admission
    pub(crate) reconciliation_running: AtomicBool,
    pub(crate) reconciliation_requested: AtomicBool,
    pub(crate) recovery_stale_producers: Mutex<Vec<(SessionId, InvocationId, ProducerId)>>,
    pub(crate) next_admission_generation: AtomicU64,
    pub(crate) admission_tasks: Mutex<Vec<JoinHandle<()>>>,
    pub(crate) admission_blocking_tasks: Mutex<Vec<JoinHandle<()>>>,
    pub(crate) admission_tasks_closing: AtomicBool,

docs.title: Persistent Daemon, Dial-in Runtimes, and Runtime Capabilities
docs.text: Status: implemented (decisions of 2026-10-16 below and in Review; see Implementation notes). Checked by hand against labpc on 2026-10-20: an ssh template and a dial-in runtime, the daemon built from 85710393d and the remote runtime from the b2ddb9e72 musl release build; every check passed. This spec extends the runtimes spec; where they differ, this one governs.

docs.title: 1. Goal and scope
docs.text:
Today the daemon is tied to the directory it starts in: that directory keys its session store and is its local runtime's workspace. A runtime is a process the daemon spawns for one workspace, and it offers one set of tools. This spec changes three things:

  1. Persistent processes. The daemon and a runtime can each run as a long-lived process holding many active sessions: a daemon serves sessions of any directory, and one runtime process serves every workspace its sessions use, concurrently.
  2. Runtime lifetimes and capabilities. A runtime is either short-lived or persistent, with one runtime protocol for both. A runtime offers several capabilities, such as coding and computer_use, and sessions attach and detach each one separately.
  3. Client runtimes. A client can offer a runtime that ends when the client does.

Decided 2026-10-16:

  • The persistent daemon is explicit: cookie daemon plus cookie attach --url --token. There is no discovery file or autostart, and plain cookie keeps running the daemon in-process.
  • The daemon can listen beyond loopback, so runtimes and clients on other machines connect to it directly.
  • A persistent runtime dials the daemon and registers itself; the daemon does not dial runtimes.
  • Every runtime, spawned or dial-in, serves all of its sessions, workspaces, and capabilities concurrently over one connection; the daemon never opens a second connection to the same runtime.
  • A client runtime is not a protocol feature: a client that offers a runtime embeds a dial-in runtime in its own process, so the runtime ends when the client process does. The client protocol knows nothing of it.
  • Any session may attach a client's runtime. While it is gone its tools vanish but attachments stay, and they come back when that runtime dials in again.
  • A TUI offers its own machine as a runtime only when the daemon is on another machine. A daemon on the same machine serves the TUI's directory with its local runtime, so sessions keep working after the TUI closes.

Out of scope: a computer-use implementation (this spec adds the mechanism and the coding and global capabilities only), daemon discovery, and resuming calls that were in flight when a connection dropped.

docs.title: 2. Vocabulary
docs.text:
Term Meaning Runtime One connection that speaks the runtime protocol and offers capabilities, identified by its runtime ID. Lifetime How the daemon gets the connection: spawned (the daemon runs a template's command over stdio and stops it with the daemon) or dial-in (the runtime connects to the daemon's /runtime endpoint). A dial-in runtime is persistent when it runs as its own service (cookie runtime serve --daemon), and short-lived when a client embeds it. Both speak the same protocol once connected. Capability A named set of tools and context a runtime offers, such as coding or computer_use. It declares a free-form kind label and whether it takes a workspace. Capability instance A capability opened for one workspace (or none): (runtime ID, capability, canonical workspace). It replaces the runtimes spec's runtime instance. Sessions attached to it share it. Attachment A durable session fact binding the session to a capability instance under a session-unique attachment name.

The global runtime offers one capability, global. The local runtime offers coding. The daemon never branches on a runtime's or capability's kind; it reads what capabilities report.

docs.title: 3. Daemon
docs.text:
• Sessions of any directory. session.create takes the client's cwd. It is stamped as the session's cwd_identity, so session.list with that identity shows the sessions of the client's directory, and it is the default workspace of the session's coding attachment. Without cwd the daemon's own directory is used, as today. The store stays where it is (sessions/<daemon workdirkey>/).
  • local serves any workspace on the daemon's machine: it opens a coding instance per workspace a session asks for, in the daemon's process.
  • Persistence. cookie daemon keeps sessions, runs, background calls, and runtimes going while no client is attached, as it does today. Plain cookie is unchanged.
  • Listening. cookie daemon --listen <addr:port> binds any address; loopback stays the default. --tls-cert and --tls-key serve wss. TLS is supported, not required: without it the token crosses the network in the clear, which the guide says plainly, so a plaintext listener off loopback belongs on a private network such as a VPN.
  • One durable token. The bearer token is [server] token in config.toml, written there at the daemon's first start when missing, so it survives restarts. Clients and dial-in runtimes present the same token, read from their machine's configuration unless given --token.
  • Endpoints. /ws for clients and /runtime for dial-in runtimes.

docs.title: 4. Runtime protocol 5: capabilities
docs.text:
runtime/initialize describes the runtime; capability instances are opened separately, so one connection serves every workspace and capability its sessions use. Today one connection holds one workspace's tools, MCP servers, and skills, fixed at initialize, and the daemon keys connections by (runtime ID, workspace); that is all that ties a runtime process to one workspace. Calls already run concurrently on one connection.

runtime/initialize. Params keep version, runtime_id, and settings (tool output, AGENTS.md, and, for a spawned runtime, the template's MCP servers) and lose workspace. The result keeps version and platform and replaces kind, attachment_name, workspace, tools, and skills with:

Result field Meaning capabilities [{ name, kind, takes_workspace, description }]: what the runtime offers. name matches [a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}.

New messages:

Method Direction Purpose capability/open daemon → runtime { capability, workspace? } → { instance, attachment_name, workspace?, tools, skills }. Opening an instance that is already open returns it. A workspace is required exactly when the capability takes one. capability/tools_changed runtime → daemon { instance, tools }; replaces runtime/tools_changed.

instance is a runtime-chosen string, unique on its connection. tool/prepare, runtime/context, mcp/changed, and mcp/reconnect gain instance. Prepared IDs stay unique per connection, so tool/execute, revalidate, release, cancel, progress, and detachable are unchanged.

MCP servers. A capability that hosts MCP (the coding capability does) runs its runtime's MCP servers in each of its instances, in that instance's workspace, as today. A spawned runtime gets them from its template; a dial-in runtime reads its own machine's configuration (section 5).

Producers. A runtime produces as source runtime:<runtime ID> and may address any session attached to any of its instances (today: runtime:<attachment name>, attached sessions of one instance).

Spawned runtimes. One process per template serves all its instances. The {workspace} command placeholder goes. cookie runtime coding --stdio becomes cookie runtime serve --stdio, offering every built-in capability; --root <dir> (repeatable) limits the workspaces coding opens.

docs.title: 5. Dial-in runtimes
docs.text:
• cookie runtime serve --daemon <url> --id <runtime ID> connects to the daemon's /runtime endpoint and presents the token and its runtime ID. The daemon then drives the protocol exactly as for a spawned runtime: runtime/initialize, then capability/open for every attachment its sessions hold.
  • No template. A dial-in runtime chooses its own ID, which must match no [runtimes.<id>] template and no connected runtime. It runs on its own machine, so it takes its MCP servers from that machine's [runtime.mcp.servers] configuration rather than from the daemon's.
  • Reconnect. A dial-in runtime reconnects with backoff for as long as its process runs. While it is away its instances are reconnecting and their tools are absent; attachments stay, and a runtime that dials in again under the same ID gets them back. It keeps its own state across reconnects (background work it tracks, producer recovery). As implemented (see phase 3), its instances follow the reconnect policy instead: their tools stay published while they are reconnecting, and leave the tool lists only once the instances become failed, after about 7 seconds.

docs.title: 6. Client runtimes
docs.text:
A client offers a runtime by running a dial-in runtime in its own process, with the client's token; it is section 5 with nothing added. When the client exits, the connection drops and the runtime is gone.

TUI. The daemon's handshake result gains machine_id, a hash that identifies its machine. A TUI attached to a daemon with another machine_id dials in a runtime client_<hostname> offering coding, and its new sessions attach it at the TUI's directory instead of local. A TUI on the daemon's machine offers nothing.

docs.title: 7. Sessions and attachments
docs.text:
• Attach targets name a capability: { runtime_id, capability, workspace? }. RuntimeAttached gains capability (additive: an older event reads as global for the global runtime and coding otherwise).
  • The attachment name comes from capability/open: global; <runtime ID>_<workspace basename> for coding; a capability without a workspace names itself, such as labpc_computer_use.
  • Default attachments of session.create: global, and coding at the session's cwd on local (or on the TUI's runtime, section 6).
  • An attachment whose runtime is not connected contributes no tools, and sessions see a notice, as for a failed instance today. Attaching a runtime that is not connected fails.

docs.title: 8. Client protocol 45
docs.text:
• session.create takes cwd; its runtimes entries and session.runtime.attach take capability.
  • runtimes.list returns runtimes (runtime_id, lifetime (spawned or dial_in), connection status, capabilities) and instances (runtime_id, capability, workspace, attachment_name, status). runtimes.reconnect restarts a spawned runtime; a dial-in runtime reconnects itself.
  • The handshake result gains machine_id.
  • The TUI's /runtime panel lists runtimes with their capabilities and attaches a capability, with a workspace when it takes one.

docs.title: 9. Phases
docs.text:
Each phase lands as its own commits with every gate green, and is pushed.

  1. Capabilities. Runtime protocol 5, one process per spawned runtime serving every workspace, capability attachments, global and coding as capabilities, client protocol 45, the /runtime panel.
  2. Directory-independent daemon. session.create cwd, local serving any workspace, cookie attach sending its directory.
  3. Listening and dial-in. --listen, optional TLS, the durable token, the /runtime endpoint, cookie runtime serve --daemon, reconnect.
  4. TUI runtime. machine_id and the TUI's embedded runtime when the daemon is remote.
  5. Documentation. Runtime guide and protocol references; the runtimes spec points here.

docs.title: 10. Review
docs.text:
Confirmed in review 2026-10-16:

  • The store stays keyed by the daemon's directory; sessions are told apart by cwd_identity, the client's cwd.
  • Producers produce as runtime:<runtime ID>.
  • machine_id decides whether a TUI offers its machine.
  • Computer use is mechanism only.
  • A call in flight when its runtime's connection drops fails with runtime_unavailable.
  • The daemon listens on any address; TLS is supported, not required.
  • Clients and dial-in runtimes share one durable token.
  • Dial-in runtimes choose their own IDs and bring their own MCP configuration.
  • Spawned runtimes stay, as the short-lived way to start a runtime (for example over ssh), but like every runtime one connection serves all their sessions: one process per template, no {workspace} placeholder, and --root limits the workspaces coding opens.

docs.title: 11. Implementation notes
docs.text:
Phase 1 (2026-10-16): runtime protocol 5 and client protocol 45.

  • capability/close is not part of the protocol: an instance stays open for its connection's life, as runtime instances did.
  • capability is optional where a session attaches or retries: without it the runtime's only capability is used, and a runtime that offers several asks for one. This keeps attaching a runtime that has not connected yet a single step.
  • runtimes.list also reports a runtime's last connection failure (message), since an attach that names no capability has no instance to mark failed.
  • Plugins keep runtime/tools_changed and send no instance: a plugin connection has one implicit instance.
  • cookie runtime coding --workspace became cookie runtime serve --stdio [--root <dir>]....

Phase 2 (2026-10-16): the TUI binary passes its canonical directory, so both plain cookie and cookie attach create sessions for it and list only its sessions; a session list without a directory (tests, other clients) shows every session.

Phase 3 (2026-10-16): cookie daemon --listen, --tls-cert/--tls-key, --token-file; the /runtime endpoint; cookie runtime serve --daemon --id.

  • A dial-in runtime hosts the MCP servers of [runtimes.local.mcp] in its own machine's configuration, rather than a new [runtime.mcp] table: on that machine, those are the servers its local runtime hosts.
  • While a dial-in runtime is away, its instances follow the reconnect policy (reconnecting, then failed, their tools dropped); dialing in again reopens every failed one.
  • The daemon no longer checks that a client's address is loopback: the token is the gate, and the listener decides who can reach it.

Phase 4 (2026-10-16): ServerHello.machine_id (a SHA-256 of the OS machine ID, or of a per-user random ID where there is none); cookie attach to a daemon with another machine ID dials in client_<host name>, limited to the TUI's directory with --root, and the TUI's sessions attach it.

  • The embedded runtime is limited to the TUI's directory rather than offering the whole machine to a remote daemon.
  • Machine IDs fall back to a per-user file, so two users of one machine without an OS machine ID look like two machines.

Token (2026-10-17): at the user's request the durable token lives in [server] token of config.toml instead of a --token-file. The daemon writes a fresh one there at its first start when there is none and never regenerates it; clients and dial-in runtimes read it from their machine's configuration when given no --token.

Daemon address (2026-10-17): [server] url names the daemon clients and dial-in runtimes connect to, defaulting to the local daemon the same table describes. cookie runtime serve --daemon takes the URL optionally and --id defaults to the sanitized host name, so a configured machine dials in with cookie runtime serve --daemon; --url, --token, and the URL after --daemon override the configuration.

docs.title: Runtimes: Daemon, Global Runtime, and Coding Runtimes
docs.text:
Status: implemented (all four phases, product decisions approved 2026-10-15); the manual end-to-end check against labpc that phase 4 names passed on 2026-10-20: an ssh template and a dial-in runtime, the daemon built from 85710393d and the remote runtime from the b2ddb9e72 musl release build. This document is the governing specification for splitting tool execution and workspace context out of the engine into attachable runtimes. Section Open questions lists anything still undecided.

The runtime capabilities spec later changed parts of this one: a runtime offers capabilities over one connection that serves every workspace (runtime protocol 5), instances are keyed by (runtime ID, capability, workspace), templates no longer substitute {workspace}, runtimes can dial in, and the daemon serves sessions of any directory. Where the two differ, that spec governs.

docs.title: 1. Goal and scope
docs.text:
Cookie Agent aims to cover both coding-agent use (opencode) and personal assistant use (openclaw). Both need the agent's tools to live somewhere other than the process that runs the model loop: a session may work in a repository on another machine, in several workspaces at once, or with no workspace at all.

Today the daemon is a workspace. EngineOptions.cwd locates the session store, roots permission paths, resolves relative tool paths, feeds the <working_directory> prompt block, finds AGENTS.md and project skills, and selects the workspace configuration layer. The built-in tools are constructed once for that directory.

After this work the processes split three ways:

clients (TUI, CLI, later others)
   │  client protocol (WebSocket / in-memory)
daemon = gateway
   │  config, agents, sessions, model loop, permissions, approvals,
   │  delegation, goals, messaging, compaction, artifacts
   │  base layer tools · global runtime (in-process)
   │  runtime protocol (stdio / in-memory)
coding runtimes, one per workspace (local in-process, remote via a command)

In scope (the milestone): the runtime seam, session attachments, the runtime protocol, and remote coding runtimes launched by command. The milestone ends when a session on the local daemon works in a repository on another machine (labpc over ssh) end to end.

Out of scope: a persistent or discoverable daemon, runtimes that dial in, channel adapters (chat apps), schedulers and other openclaw-style triggers, web clients, and runtime kinds other than coding. Producer messages are the only notification path, and in this milestone they stayed a daemon-side plugin feature; runtime protocol 4 later opened them to runtimes (see external producers).

docs.title: 2. Vocabulary
docs.text: Term Meaning Daemon Today's daemon, unchanged in process model: plain cookie runs it in-process, cookie daemon serves it over WebSocket. It is the gateway. Its working directory now only locates the session store and stamps cwd_identity. Base layer Tools the daemon implements itself for its own orchestration. Always present, never detachable. Runtime A source of tools, workspace context, and producer messages. Runtime kind A free-form label a runtime declares for itself in runtime/initialize, such as global or coding; templates do not declare it. The daemon only displays it: behaviour follows from what a runtime reports (its workspace, tools, and skills), never from its kind, so runtimes of new kinds need no daemon change. Runtime template A configured way to start runtimes: [runtimes.<id>]. The <id> is the runtime ID. Runtime instance A running runtime: one per (runtime ID, canonical workspace). Shared by every session attached to it. Attachment A durable session fact binding a session to a runtime instance under a session-unique attachment name. Attachment name The name the runtime instance reports for itself in runtime/initialize; used as the tool prefix on collisions. Model-facing text calls this an attachment (see the memory spec). Machine The computer a runtime runs on; the daemon groups runtimes into machines. Added by the memory spec.

docs.title: 3. Layers
docs.text:
Layer Runs in Tools Context Base layer daemon delegate_subagent, get_subagent_result, send_message, skill, goal_get, goal_update, read_artifact (new), stop_background none Global runtime (global) daemon process, in-process trait calls top-level [mcp] servers and [plugins], webfetch (declared Fallback), memory tools (memory spec) user skills (~/.agents/skills, ~/.cookie-agent/skills), memory snapshot Coding runtime (coding) built-in local instance in the daemon process; others in child processes read, write, edit, bash, webfetch, plus MCP servers from its template workspace root, platform, AGENTS.md, project skills

Plugins exist only on the daemon, hosted by the global runtime. Hosting MCP servers is up to each runtime, not part of the runtime contract: coding runtimes host them, and a runtime that does not rejects a template that lists some. No runtime hosts plugins.

Rules:

  • The global runtime never offers read, write, edit, or bash. Those exist only where a coding runtime is attached.
  • Every daemon always has the local coding runtime template for its own working directory. There is no flag to disable it.
  • New sessions attach global and local (the daemon's working directory) by default. A session may detach either. A session with no coding runtime is valid: it has the base layer and whatever the global runtime offers.
  • Artifact reads move from read to the base layer's read_artifact { artifact, stream?, offset, limit }, so a session with no coding runtime can still page through retained output. artifact is the 64-hex digest and stream an optional stream name; the model-facing artifact://<digest>[/<stream>] URI form is removed. Truncation hints read read_artifact(artifact="<digest>", stream="stdout", offset=…). read becomes filesystem-only. The persisted artifact://sha256/<digest> form in ArtifactReference is internal and unchanged.
  • read_artifact needs no permission rule: it can only reach the session tree's own artifacts. The read: {"artifact://*": allow} pattern and the artifact:// pass-through in permission resource resolution go away.

docs.title: 4.1 Templates
docs.text:
[runtimes.labpc]
command = ["ssh", "labpc", "cookie", "runtime", "coding", "--stdio", "--workspace", "{workspace}"]
env = { }                     # additions to the inherited environment
startup_timeout_ms = 10000
shutdown_grace_ms = 3000

[runtimes.labpc.mcp.servers.rust_analyzer]
command = "rust-analyzer-mcp"
  • Runtime IDs match [a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31} because they become tool-name prefixes. global and local are reserved.
  • [runtimes.local] may exist without command; it only carries the mcp table for the built-in local coding runtime. Any other template requires a nonempty command. Templates accept no plugins table.
  • Templates do not declare a kind. The command decides what runs, and the runtime reports its kind in runtime/initialize, so there is one source of truth. The mcp table is still parsed strictly when the configuration loads; a runtime that hosts no MCP servers rejects a nonempty one at initialize.
  • A template whose command contains {workspace} needs a workspace: attach and session creation require one. A template without the placeholder takes none, and supplying one is an error.
  • {workspace} is substituted as one whole argv element, with no shell interpretation by cookie. A command that reaches a remote shell (ssh) is responsible for quoting; the reference docs must say so.
  • The child inherits the daemon's environment plus env, because ssh needs SSH_AUTH_SOCK and similar variables.
  • Template MCP servers are sent to the runtime in runtime/initialize and run on the runtime's machine. MCP OAuth stays global-runtime-only (its credential store is the daemon's mcp-oauth.json); a template server with oauth enabled fails validation. Static-header HTTP servers are allowed.
  • Top-level [mcp] and [plugins] keep their current meaning and belong to the global runtime.
  • Plugin environment changes: plugins, like MCP servers and runtimes, now inherit the daemon's environment, and env adds to it instead of replacing it. This drops today's env_clear(), so a plugin also sees provider API keys that the daemon reads from its environment.

docs.title: 4.2 Removed
docs.text:
• The workspace configuration layer: <cwd>/.cookie-agent/config.toml and <cwd>/.cookie-agent/agents/ are no longer read. Configuration is the user layer only. config_paths.workspace, workspace_mcp_servers, McpConfigTarget::WorkspaceFile, the TUI's "project config.toml" MCP target, and AgentDocumentSource::Workspace go away.
  • BuiltinTools::new(workspace): coding tools take their workspace from the runtime instance.
  • The lazy MCP server setting and the lazy-not-connected status. Every enabled server connects eagerly (section 6.4); an authored lazy key is an unknown field.

No migration or compatibility decoder is added (see AGENTS.md). A leftover workspace file is ignored silently because it is simply never opened; the docs say so. AGENTS.md files under .cookie-agent/agents/ are context, not configuration, and keep working (section 8).

docs.title: 5.1 Events (additive, versionless)
docs.text:
• RuntimeAttached { name, runtime_id, kind, workspace } where workspace is the canonical path the runtime reported (absent for global).
  • RuntimeDetached { name }.

A session's attachment set is the fold of these events. SessionCreated stays as it is; creation writes one RuntimeAttached per initial attachment in the same append. A session whose log holds no RuntimeAttached or RuntimeDetached event at all was created before this change and is read as attached to global and local.

docs.title: 5.2 Operations
docs.text:
• Attach and detach are accepted only while the session has no active run (SessionRunning otherwise), so the set is fixed for every run.
  • Creating a session or attaching a runtime connects it eagerly (section 6.4). Attach waits for the instance to start and for runtime/initialize; failure rejects the attach and records nothing.
  • The runtime chooses its attachment name and returns it from runtime/initialize; clients do not supply one. The global runtime returns global. A coding runtime returns <runtime ID>_<workspace basename>, with the basename lowercased, every character outside [a-z0-9_] replaced by _, repeats collapsed, and the result capped at 32 bytes: labpc in ~/cookie-agent is labpc_cookie_agent. Because the name is fixed per instance, it is the same in every session that attaches that instance.
  • If a session already has an attachment with the returned name (two workspaces with the same basename), the daemon appends _2, _3, and so on for that session.
  • Delegated children inherit the parent's attachments. delegate_subagent accepts an optional runtimes list of the parent's attachment names that narrows the child's set. The child's log records its own RuntimeAttached events so the child is self-describing. Changed 2026-10-17: the runtimes argument is gone; every delegated child inherits the root session's attachments.
  • Reopening a session in a daemon that does not have its instances running (after a restart, or a session created by another daemon) connects them when the session is opened, with the same rules as creation.

docs.title: 6. Tool composition
docs.text: The model's tool list should change as rarely as possible: every change costs the provider's prompt cache and can confuse a model that has already called a tool by name.

docs.title: 6.1 Minimal change, not frozen
docs.text:
The tool set is not frozen. As today, published_tool_definitions recomputes it on every model turn. Instead, the sources of change are reduced so that the list only changes when something really appeared or went away:

  • no lazy connections: everything a session can use is connected when the session is created or opened (section 6.4);
  • short disconnects are bridged by reconnecting before any tool is dropped (section 6.4);
  • only real collisions rename tools (section 6.3).

What remains is the user attaching or detaching a runtime, an MCP server or runtime that cannot be reached at all, and an MCP server changing its own tool list.

docs.title: 6.2 Collision enum
docs.text:
Every runtime tool declares collision: prefix | fallback (default prefix).

  • prefix: on a collision the tool is published as <attachment>_<name>.
  • fallback: on a collision the tool is hidden. The global runtime's webfetch uses this.

Base layer names are reserved: a runtime tool with a base name is always treated as colliding.

docs.title: 6.3 Collisions
docs.text:
Names are computed from the current tool set every time it is composed:

  • A name offered by exactly one source is published bare.
  • When several prefix tools offer one name, the bare name is removed and each of them is published as <attachment>_<name>.
