  • Re-rendering. The page re-renders only items whose item_key (the item's version, its tools' revisions, expansion, and the level filter) changed.
  • Highlighting. highlight.js 11.12.0 is vendored with its BSD-3-Clause licence and checked against the npm sha512 integrity, with no CDN.
  • It is copied by Trunk and loaded on the first code block that names its language, through js_sys calls.
  • Its token colours come from the palette, light and dark.
  • Serving.
  • web_assets' build script gzips each compressible file. The daemon sends that copy when Accept-Encoding takes gzip, with Vary: Accept-Encoding and an ETag of its own. Brotli is left out: it would need another crate, and gzip covers every browser.
  • CSP. Every response carries a Content-Security-Policy:
    • script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval' plus a hash of Trunk's inline loader, computed at build time;
    • connect-src 'self' ws: wss:;
    • img-src and media-src with blob:;
    • style-src 'unsafe-inline', which inline terminal colours need;
    • no objects, base URI, framing, or form targets.
  • Size. The bundle is 4.28 MB, 1.65 MB gzipped. Of that, the wasm is 3.88 MB (1.40 MB gzipped), highlight.js 43 KB gzipped, and the fonts 187 KB.
  • scripts/build-web.sh now fails over a budget of 1,900,000 bytes gzipped, which CI enforces in the web job.
  • Tests.
  • Native web tests:
    • every block kind's HTML;
    • markdown sanitization (raw HTML escaped, javascript: links neutralized, images as links, code language classes);
    • SGR to spans;
    • diff line numbers;
    • the composer key mapping and the slash commands;
    • the event-level filter and item keys.
  • client_state tests: every transition of the subscription machine, and the mode cycle.
  • Server tests: gzip negotiation and revalidation of the compressed copy, and the CSP on every response.

  • scripts/test-web-page.sh. It now runs a scripted OpenAI-compatible model (scripts/web-e2e/mock-model.py) behind a daemon whose agent asks before bash. scripts/web-e2e/scenarios.py drives headless Firefox through:

    • connecting from the cookie web link;
    • a new session with streamed, highlighted markdown;
    • a tool call approved from the approvals sheet, with its terminal output;
    • steering a slow run, queueing behind it with Alt+Enter, and cancelling it with Escape, after which the unsent messages return to the composer;
    • a 375 px window with no sideways scroll and the sessions sheet;
    • the origin hint from a daemon that allows no origin.

    All pass, and the screenshots were checked. - Not in CI yet. The browser scenarios still need Firefox and geckodriver in CI (W5).

docs.title: Phase W3 (2026-10-20)
docs.text:
Session depth landed as specified, with no wire change.

  • Moved into shared crates.
  • cookie_agent_protocol::media_sniff. Recognizing and validating media from its content (validate_upload, the image, PDF, audio, and video checks, the caps) moved out of runtime_api::media, which re-exports it. The page sniffs a file exactly as the daemon will.
  • client_state::permissions: the /permissions table rows (permission_rows, permission_actions, the effect and source labels) and a draft's rules (set_draft_rule, remove_draft_rule). The TUI uses them.
  • client_state::uploads. upload now returns an UploadFailure whose too_large carries the limits a media_too_large refusal names (RefusedLimits), so the page can offer a downscale to them. The TUI keeps showing the message.
  • SessionState::user_files: the files each user message attached, by its sequence, for inline display.
  • The page (crates/web/src/workspace/, views/depth.rs):
  • Subagents. The Agents panel in the sidebar (and the sessions sheet) shows the viewed session's session.tree, foldable per session, with /agent-panel show|hide|auto as in the TUI: auto shows it while a delegate is live or a child is viewed.
    • The tree is re-read on tool_call_linked, run_finished, delegation_progressed, delegation_finished, delegate_child_terminated, and a finished replay of any session in it.
    • Its live sessions are subscribed, sharing the root's ownership.
    • A session_ref or tree row opens the child. Its root comes from the shown tree, the session list, or session.get's origin.
  • History edits. A user message's ⋯ menu copies it (navigator.clipboard, else the text is selected), reverts to before it (session.revert with expected_last_seq, confirmed first; the rewound notification rebuilds the transcript and the text returns to the composer; stale_revert is explained), or forks at it (session.fork with a client_fork_id, then opens the fork). /compact [focus] compacts; Escape and /cancel cancel a compaction outside a run (session.compact.cancel).
  • Goal. The goal bar shows the root's goal with the actions its status allows. /goal <objective> sets it with the draft's selection; /goal pause|resume|cancel reads session.goal.get and changes it at its revision. Goals are root-only and read-only snapshots offer none. Only goal_* events change the bar.
  • Background. A running call with backgroundable offers "⇲ background" (run.tool_background). session.background.list is read after each subscribe and background.changed keeps it current. The bar and the /background sheet list the calls with their age and stop one (session.background.stop); the sheet closes with the last call.
  • Media. /attach and 📎 open a file input whose accept lists the selected model's input_media types; 📷 (narrow screens, image models only) opens one with capture. Drop and paste attach too. Nothing is offered for a model without input media.
    • Each file is sniffed and checked against the model (attach::assess), then uploaded at once through the shared chunked upload (a new session is created first, as in the TUI), and shown as a chip.
    • An image over the model's or the daemon's limits, or refused by the daemon as media_too_large, is offered "Downscale and attach?". It is decoded and redrawn through a canvas, as JPEG when the model takes it (else PNG), at the size attach::downscale_target computes, and smaller again until it fits. Video is never re-encoded.
    • Attachments of user messages and media_file parts of assistant messages render inline through the same artifact.read → Blob placeholders as media blocks.
  • Skills. /skills [search] lists skills.list, ranked as the TUI ranks them (skills::matching_skills). Running one checks it with skills.get, then submits encode_skill_submission.
  • Permissions. /permissions shows the effective rules by action with their source. An effect click or the new-rule form sets an override (session.permission.set), and × clears one. While a new session is composed, the same table edits the draft's rules, previewed with session.permission.preview and sent as permission_rules on session.create.
  • /events default. The level the page starts with is the TUI's (EventLevel::DEFAULT_MINIMUM, warnings), so [I] rows are hidden by default; a stored choice still wins.
  • Fixes found on the way.
  • Item keys include the session. Item IDs repeat across sessions, so switching between two sessions of the same shape showed the first one's cached rows.
  • Following the transcript. It stops only when the user scrolls up (wheel, touch, or the scrollbar), not when a re-rendered row or a new bar briefly moves the scroll position.
  • Deviations.
  • /goal pause|resume|cancel are typed arguments. The TUI's palette asks only for an objective and puts the controls on the bar; the page has both.
  • The skill arguments, compaction focus, and goal objective are typed after the command (/skills gre, /compact keep the API notes), or in the sheet, instead of a palette step.
  • Fork and revert are offered on any user message the session's owner can edit, child sessions included, as the daemon decides what is allowed.
  • Size. Profiled with twiggy on an unstripped web build, the wasm was mostly serde code, plus two things the page never needed:
  • regex, used only for the control-character table in diagnostics. It is now a hand-written table, checked against the regex in a native test.
  • Runtime schema generation, used by open_enum! to list a tagged enum's tags. The tags are now listed in each open_enum! and checked against the schema in a native test.

Together they were about 1 MB of the wasm: before W3 it was 3.88 MB (1.40 MB gzipped), and without them 2.85 MB (1.06 MB gzipped). With all of W3 it is 3.19 MB (1.20 MB gzipped), and the bundle 3.60 MB (1.45 MB gzipped). The budget in scripts/build-web.sh is now 1,600,000 bytes gzipped (from 1,900,000). - Tests. - Native: tree rows and folding and the auto panel; /goal arguments and the bar's actions; skill ranking; the accept list, the assessment of a file (attach, downscale, refuse), downscale targets and refused-limit tightening; attachment names; the permission rows and draft rules; user_files; session-scoped item keys; the slash commands with arguments. - scripts/test-web-page.sh now gives the daemon a model that takes images, a helper subagent, a greet skill, an image in the workspace, and a session made by cookie run before the daemon started. The scenarios add: - a delegation shown in the Agents panel (/agent-panel show), its session_ref opening the child, and folding; - a fork at the first message and a revert of the last, with its text back in the composer; - /compact with a focus; - /goal set, then paused from the bar; - a slow bash call approved, moved to the background, listed with /background, and stopped; - an image attached from the file input, and one too large downscaled on acceptance, both shown inline in the sent message; - a read of an image whose media block shows inline; - /skills search and run; - a session permission override added and removed, and a draft rule previewed for a new session; - the cookie run session, whose owner lock the scenario holds as another process would, opening as a read-only snapshot.

All pass, and the screenshots were checked.

docs.title: Phase W4 (2026-10-20)
docs.text:
Management landed as specified, with no wire change.

  • Moved into cookie_agent_client_state, with the TUI switched over:
  • runtimes: attachment rows matched to their instances, a new session's draft runtimes, the attach choices and their search, the attach and retry requests, the machines view's rows, the machine actions each row offers, the changes they make, and their status lines.
  • mcp: the server order, which servers mcp.server.* edits, a server form as text and the definition it makes (McpFields), and the labels.
  • providers: a provider row's state, the model-availability and catalog lines, the setup values and credentials a connect sends, and the store-contention policy. Credentials are serialized once from the caller's buffers into a zeroized buffer (credential_values), as the TUI did.
  • config: the document rows, a new agent's template and path rules, and what an apply or reload answered and what the panel says about it.
  • memory: the rows by layer and group, a new memory's template and URL rules, what a write answered, and a refused delete's message.
  • plugins: a plugin's state and details, and its events' status line.
  • tool_header and rows: a tool call's header text, which drops an argument its title already names, the hint icons, and the producer and goal row labels.
  • The page (crates/web/src/workspace/manage.rs, crates/web/src/views/manage.rs):
  • /runtime: the session's attachments with their status, attach (search, then a workspace when needed), detach, and retry (runtimes.reconnect). In a new session, the draft's runtimes start as global and local's coding at the chosen directory (else where the daemon's own coding instance works, from runtimes.list). Each opens at once, and session.create attaches them. The Machines tab renames, merges, forgets, assigns, and unassigns. The panel re-reads runtimes.list and machines.list every second while open, as the TUI polls, and on runtimes.changed and machines.changed.
  • /mcp: the servers in the TUI's order with state, tools, source, and error, and add, edit, enable or disable, remove, reconnect, and persist. A server that needs authorization says to run cookie mcp auth <server> or use the TUI. Polled every second while open, and on mcp.changed.
  • /connect: the catalog's providers with their state, a connect form per auth method with password fields for credentials, and disconnect with its confirmation. Connects go through connect_provider_retrying, and disconnects retry once on store contention, as in the TUI.
  • /config: the documents, an in-page monospace editor, config.apply at the revision and fingerprint read, refused edits kept to fix, conflicts dropped and reloaded, new agent documents, delete, and config.reload.
  • /memory: the memories by layer, an in-page editor, writes at the revision read, the invalid and changed outcomes with their choices (edit again, reload, overwrite, drop), create, and delete with its revision. It refreshes on memory.changed and machines.changed.
  • /plugins: state and details, restart, plugins.changed, and events.plugin status lines for the viewed session.
  • From the W3 review: producer messages (goal control and reminders, background-call and subagent reports) render as the TUI renders them. A claimed or consumed one is a folded line with its summary that opens to its owner, delivery, and body. A pending or admitted one does not show yet, and a discarded one shows only at the debug level. Goal activations show as their /goal action and goal states as the objective, status, and checklist. Plugin messages, AGENTS.md, loaded skills, and compactions fold as in the TUI. Tool titles use the TUI's header text, so a title that names its argument does not repeat it.
  • Size. Client::call now serializes its parameters before awaiting one shared request future instead of one per parameter type, which saved 16 KB gzipped. The wasm is 3.63 MB (1.37 MB gzipped), and the bundle 4.04 MB (1.62 MB gzipped). Most of the W4 growth is each RPC's request and answer code. The budget in scripts/build-web.sh is raised to 1,700,000 bytes gzipped, with that reason recorded beside it.
  • Deviations.
  • Editors are in the page. /config and /memory edit in a text area (section 6) instead of $EDITOR. A refused config edit stays open in the editor rather than reopening on the next edit.
  • Provider rows say their state in words, without the TUI's key hints.
  • The TUI's copy changed slightly where it now shares the web's text: a refused config edit says "Not applied; edit config.toml again.", and an existing new-agent or new-memory path says "exists; edit it instead".
  • Tests.
  • Native: client_state tests for the runtime, machine, config, memory, MCP, and provider rules, the producer summary, and the tool header; web tests for the folded producer rows and the new commands.

  • scripts/test-web-page.sh now configures a runtime template that never starts ([runtimes.box]) and the reference plugin. The scenarios add:

    • a draft runtime that fails, is retried, and is removed;
    • a session's local coding attachment detached and attached again;
    • a machine renamed;
    • an MCP server that cannot start added, disabled, and removed;
    • a provider connected with an API key (which never shows on the page) and disconnected;
    • a config edit with an unknown key refused, then a valid edit applied;
    • a memory refused as invalid, created, overwritten after a change on disk, and deleted;
    • the reference plugin restarted;
    • goal-control and background-report rows folded, and one opened.

    All pass, and the screenshots were checked.

docs.title: Phase W5 (2026-10-20)
docs.text:
Phone polish, the home screen, the end-to-end suites in CI, and the documentation. There is no wire change.

  • Phones. A new audit in scripts/test-web-page.sh opens every view and sheet (the transcript, sessions, every picker, and every panel) at 360 × 640 and 390 × 844 portrait and 844 × 390 landscape. It fails on sideways scroll, a control the screen's edge cuts off, or a target under 44 px. Firefox windows are at least 500 px wide, so a narrower screen is that window with the page zoomed in, which needs geckodriver's --allow-system-access. It found, and the page now fixes:
  • the composer's Send button cut off at 360 px: the text field could not shrink. The composer now wraps its buttons below the field when the field would be narrower than 12rem;
  • buttons narrower than 44 px (attach, camera, the command menu, the send menu, the permission effects): every button has a 44 px minimum width;
  • session rows squeezed into each other in a short landscape sidebar: rows no longer shrink;
  • the header wrapping its title and buttons over three lines: shorter labels ("Forget", the theme's name) below the sm breakpoint.
  • The on-screen keyboard. The page keeps --app-height at the visual viewport's height, which a phone's keyboard shrinks while 100dvh may not, and sizes its frame and sheets from it; the viewport meta asks for interactive-widget=resizes-content and viewport-fit=cover, and the frame pads by the safe-area insets. Firefox cannot raise a keyboard, so this is checked by reading, not by a scenario.
  • Background tabs. A scenario pauses the daemon (SIGSTOP), hides and shows the tab, sees the page give up on the silent connection, resumes the daemon, and sees the page reconnect and restore its session.
  • Home screen. crates/web/assets/manifest.webmanifest (display: standalone, relative start_url and scope), icons drawn from the logo by scripts/web-icons.py (any and maskable 192 and 512 px PNGs, the SVG, and an Apple touch icon, palette-reduced to 22 KB together), and theme-color for light and dark. Trunk copies them under their own names; the daemon serves them with no-cache, and the CSP's default-src 'self' already covers the manifest. A scenario checks the manifest's content type and that every icon it names is served.
  • CI. The web job now also installs Firefox 157.0.1 (browser-actions/setup-firefox), geckodriver 0.37.1 (checked by SHA-256), and wasm-bindgen-test-runner 0.2.126 (install-action, matching Cargo.lock; the suite checks the match), then runs scripts/test-wasm-client.sh and scripts/test-web-page.sh, uploading the scenario screenshots when a step fails. release_integrity pins these gates, and AGENTS.md lists the two suites.
  • Size. The bundle is 4.07 MB, 1.64 MB gzipped, within the 1.7 MB budget; the manifest and icons add 23 KB.
  • Docs. clients/web.md is the complete guide (phones, the home screen, and what the page does not do, besides every panel and command); engine/server.md, daemon/persistent.md, architecture.md, and the README describe the web client as it is; sections 1 to 14 of this spec now match what landed.

docs.title: Deviations across the phases
docs.text:
• Notices of plain cookie render as rows below the transcript, not in the status row (L).
  • Refused connections cannot be told apart in a browser (close code 1006, no HTTP status), so every refusal before the handshake shows the allowed_origins hint (W0a, W1). Since 2026-10-21 it is a plain hint to check the daemon URL and that the daemon is running.
  • Browser tests run in Firefox only, not Chrome (W0a, W5).
  • Caching: only files whose names carry Trunk's hash are immutable; copied files are revalidated (W1).
  • The ready line is unchanged; the page address and the empty-allowed_origins warning follow it as log lines (W1). The warning went with the allowlist on 2026-10-21.
  • Gzip only, no Brotli (W2).
  • Shared code: the subscription machine, panel rules, and labels moved to client_state over the phases; the ownership bookkeeping stayed in each client (W2–W4).
  • Commands: /approvals and /mode exist only in the page; /goal pause|resume|cancel and typed arguments replace palette steps (W2, W3).
  • Editors are in-page text areas, and a refused config edit stays open (W4).
  • The budget was 1.9 MB gzipped in W2, 1.5 MB after W3's size work, then 1.6 MB with W3's features and 1.7 MB with W4's panels, each raise with its reason recorded (W2–W4). After the UI polish of 2026-10-21 the release build (Rust 1.88.0) measured 1.75 MB, and the budget was raised to 10 MB, a backstop against runaway growth rather than a target.

docs.title: tui.toml
docs.text:
The terminal client reads ~/.cookie-agent/tui.toml independently of the engine. Both settings are optional. This is a complete file:

minimum_event_level = "warning"
theme = "auto"

There is no workspace layer, upward search, environment-selected config path, or environment interpolation. A missing file uses defaults. Unknown keys, wrong types, and malformed values fail with the path and offending key. Engine config.toml settings do not inherit into this file.

Top-level key Purpose Minimum Event Level Filter diagnostic rows Theme Select the terminal palette

These are scalar keys, not TOML tables. Omitted fields use their individual defaults; the theme's environment and terminal fallbacks are described on its page. Runtime /events palette changes are view-only and never rewrite this file. See Terminal UI for terminal operation.

docs.title: Minimum Event Level [minimum_event_level]
docs.text:
Choose which diagnostic rows appear in the conversation. Complete tui.toml:

minimum_event_level = "warning"

Accepted strings, from least to most severe, are "debug", "info", "warning", and "error". The default is "warning". Other strings and non-string values are errors. This is a top-level scalar, not a [minimum_event_level] table.

Rows below the threshold remain in the session projection. Lowering the filter to debug with the palette's /events command, or by clicking the filter in the conversation title, reveals them again. Runtime changes do not edit the file or remove events from history. There are no nested fields or workspace overrides; see tui.toml for loading behavior.

docs.title: Theme [theme]
docs.text:
Select a terminal palette. Complete tui.toml:

theme = "dark"
Value Selection "auto" Detect the terminal background, ignoring COOKIE_THEME "default" Light palette "dark" Curated dark palette "mono" Monochrome "high-contrast" Terminal-driven bright ANSI colors

Any file preference takes precedence over COOKIE_THEME, including "auto". When the key is omitted, COOKIE_THEME can select a palette; if that variable is also unset or auto, selection uses automatic detection: OSC 11, the last COLORFGBG field, and finally the light default. NO_COLOR and TERM=dumb force monochrome after selection.

Colour depth is detected separately. COLORTERM=truecolor (or 24bit) selects 24-bit colour; when COLORTERM is unset, Windows Terminal (WT_SESSION, also visible inside WSL) and TERM_PROGRAM values vscode, iTerm.app, WezTerm and ghostty count as 24-bit too. Otherwise a TERM containing 256color selects 256 colours, and anything else 16. Set COLORTERM=truecolor to opt a capable terminal in, for example over SSH, where these variables are not forwarded.

Unknown strings and non-string values fail. There are no nested fields or workspace overrides. Use the scalar theme, not a [theme] table; see tui.toml for file loading.
